p0.original: The whole of the advantages and disadvantages of the different employments of labour and stock, must, in the same neighbourhood, be either perfectly equal, or continually tending to equality. If, in the same neighbourhood, there was any employment evidently either more or less advantageous than the rest, so many people would crowd into it in the one case, and so many would desert it in the other, that its advantages would soon return to the level of other employments. This, at least, would be the case in a society where things were left to follow their natural course, where there was perfect liberty, and where every man was perfectly free both to choose what occupation he thought proper, and to change it as often as he thought proper. Every man's interest would prompt him to seek the advantageous, and to shun the disadvantageous employment.
p0.zh: 不同劳动和存量就业的全部利弊,必须在同一街区完全平等,或者继续倾向于平等。 如果在同一社区,有明显比其他就业更有利或更不利的工作,那么,在一种情况下,许多人会挤进就业,而在另一种情况下,许多人会抛弃就业,因此,就业的好处很快会回到其他就业的水平。 至少,在这样一个社会里,情况是这样的:事情要顺着自然的走向发展,那里有完美的自由,每个男人都有完全的自由,既可以选择他认为合适的职业,又可以像他认为合适的那样频繁地改变职业。每个人的利益都会促使他寻求有利者,避免不利的就业。

p1.original: Pecuniary wages and profit, indeed, are everywhere in Europe extremely different, according to the different employments of labour and stock. But this difference arises, partly from certain circumstances in the employments themselves, which, either really, or at least in the imagination of men, make up for a small pecuniary gain in some, and counterbalance a great one in others, and partly from the policy of Europe, which nowhere leaves things at perfect liberty.
p1.zh: 事实上,根据不同的劳动力和库存就业情况,欧洲各地的人均收入和利润差别很大。 但这种区别部分产生于就业本身的某些情况,这些情况实际上或至少是男人的想象力,弥补了某些人微小的金钱收益,抵消了另一些人的伟大收益,部分源于欧洲的政策,欧洲的政策使事情变得毫无自由可言。

p2.original: The particular consideration of those circumstances, and of that policy, will divide this Chapter into two parts.
p2.zh: 特别考虑这些情况和这项政策,将把本章分为两部分。

p3.original: PART I. Inequalities arising from the nature of the employments themselves.
p3.zh: 第一编就业本身的性质引起的不平等。

p4.original: The five following are the principal circumstances which, so far as I have been able to observe, make up for a small pecuniary gain in some employments, and counterbalance a great one in others. First, the agreeableness or disagreeableness of the employments themselves; secondly, the easiness and cheapness, or the difficulty and expense of learning them; thirdly, the constancy or inconstancy of employment in them; fourthly, the small or great trust which must be reposed in those who exercise them; and, fifthly, the probability or improbability of success in them.
p4.zh: 以下五个是主要的情况,就我所观察到的情况而言,这些情况弥补了某些就业的小额金钱收益,而在其他就业中,则抵消了巨大的利润。 第一,就业本身的可接受性或不满意性;第二,容易和廉价,或学习这些职业的难度和费用;第三,就业在就业中的不耐烦或不耐烦性;第四,必须重新对行使这些职业的人给予的微小或极大信任;第五,成功的可能性或不可能。

p5.original: First, the wages of labour vary with the ease or hardship, the cleanliness or dirtiness, the honourableness or dishonourableness, of the employment. Thus in most places, take the year round, a journeyman tailor earns less than a journeyman weaver. His work is much easier. A journeyman weaver earns less than a journeyman smith. His work is not always easier, but it is much cleanlier. A journeyman blacksmith, though an artificer, seldom earns so much in twelve hours, as a collier, who is only a labourer, does in eight. His work is not quite so dirty, is less dangerous, and is carried on in day-light, and above ground. Honour makes a great part of the reward of all honourable professions. In point of pecuniary gain, all things considered, they are generally under-recompensed, as I shall endeavour to shew by and by. Disgrace has the contrary effect. The trade of a butcher is a brutal and an odious business; but it is in most places more profitable than the greater part of common trades. The most detestable of all employments, that of public executioner, is, in proportion to the quantity of work done, better paid than any common trade whatever.
p5.zh: 第一,劳动工资随就业的便利或困难、清洁或肮脏、光荣或不光荣而变化。 因此,在大多数地方,一年一度,一个旅行者裁缝的收入比一个旅行者织工要少. 他的工作要简单得多。旅行者织布员的收入比旅行者铁匠还少. 他的作品并不总是更容易,但更干净。旅行铁匠,虽然是工匠,却很少在十二小时内挣这么多钱,就像一个只有工人的铁匠,在八小时内挣那么多钱一样. 他的作品并不那么肮脏,危险性较小,在白天和地面上进行.荣誉是所有荣誉职业的奖励的一部分。 就金钱利益而言,所有考虑的东西,一般都补偿不足,因为我将努力逐一抛出。毁谤有相反的效果.屠夫的买卖是残酷的,令人憎恶的生意;但在大多数地方,比一般贸易的较大部分更有利可图.在所有职业中最令人厌恶的是公共行刑者,按照所完成的工作数量的比例,报酬比任何普通贸易都要高。

p6.original: Hunting and fishing, the most important employments of mankind in the rude state of society, become, in its advanced state, their most agreeable amusements, and they pursue for pleasure what they once followed from necessity. In the advanced state of society, therefore, they are all very poor people who follow as a trade, what other people pursue as a pastime. Fishermen have been so since the time of Theocritus. {See Idyllium xxi.}. A poacher is everywhere a very poor man in Great Britain. In countries where the rigour of the law suffers no poachers, the licensed hunter is not in a much better condition. The natural taste for those employments makes more people follow them, than can live comfortably by them; and the produce of their labour, in proportion to its quantity, comes always too cheap to market, to afford any thing but the most scanty subsistence to the labourers.
p6.zh: 狩猎和捕鱼是人类在社会无礼状态中最重要的职业,在社会先进状态下,成为他们最受欢迎的娱乐,他们追求他们从必要而来的追求快乐。 因此,在社会先进状态下,他们都是作为贸易而追求的非常贫困的人,而其他人则作为消遣而追求的.渔夫们从Theocritus时代就开始这样了。 {见Idylium xxi.} 大不列颠的穷人 到处都是偷猎者 在法律严谨没有偷猎者的国家,持照猎人的状况并不好得多。对这些就业的自然品味使得更多的人跟随他们,他们无法安心地生活;而他们的劳力产品,按其数量的比例来看,总是过于廉价,无法进入市场,除了给工人提供最微薄的生计之外,任何东西都买不起。

p7.original: Disagreeableness and disgrace affect the profits of stock in the same manner as the wages of labour. The keeper of an inn or tavern, who is never master of his own house, and who is exposed to the brutality of every drunkard, exercises neither a very agreeable nor a very creditable business. But there is scarce any common trade in which a small stock yields so great a profit.
p7.zh: 不平等和耻辱以与劳动工资相同的方式影响股票利润。客栈或酒馆的保管者,从来就是自己家的主人,也暴露在每一个酒鬼的残暴之下,既不锻炼一个非常讨人喜欢的生意,也不进行非常值得称道的生意. 但是,很少有任何普通贸易,小股的利润如此之大。

p8.original: Secondly, the wages of labour vary with the easiness and cheapness, or the difficulty and expense, of learning the business.
p8.zh: 第二,劳动工资随学习企业的轻松和廉价,或困难和费用而变化。

p9.original: When any expensive machine is erected, the extraordinary work to be performed by it before it is worn out, it must be expected, will replace the capital laid out upon it, with at least the ordinary profits. A man educated at the expense of much labour and time to any of those employments which require extraordinary dexterity and skill, may be compared to one of those expensive machines. The work which he learns to perform, it must be expected, over and above the usual wages of common labour, will replace to him the whole expense of his education, with at least the ordinary profits of an equally valuable capital. It must do this too in a reasonable time, regard being had to the very uncertain duration of human life, in the same manner as to the more certain duration of the machine.
p9.zh: 当任何昂贵的机器被树立起来时,它将要完成的非常的工作在它被磨损之前,必须预料到,它将会取代它所投入的资本,至少会用普通的利润来代替它.以牺牲大量劳动和时间为代价教育任何需要非常灵活和技能的工作的人,可以与这些昂贵的机器之一相比。 他所学的工作,除了通常的普通劳动工资之外,必须期望它能够取代他的全部教育费用,至少可以取代同样有价值资本的普通利润。 它也必须在合理的时间内这样做,考虑到人类生命的极不确定的期间,与机器的更确定的期限一样。

p10.original: The difference between the wages of skilled labour and those of common labour, is founded upon this principle.
p10.zh: 技术工人的工资与普通工人的工资之间的差别就是基于这一原则的。

p11.original: The policy of Europe considers the labour of all mechanics, artificers, and manufacturers, as skilled labour; and that of all country labourers us common labour. It seems to suppose that of the former to be of a more nice and delicate nature than that of the latter. It is so perhaps in some cases; but in the greater part it is quite otherwise, as I shall endeavour to shew by and by. The laws and customs of Europe, therefore, in order to qualify any person for exercising the one species of labour, impose the necessity of an apprenticeship, though with different degrees of rigour in different places. They leave the other free and open to every body. During the continuance of the apprenticeship, the whole labour of the apprentice belongs to his master. In the meantime he must, in many cases, be maintained by his parents or relations, and, in almost all cases, must be clothed by them. Some money, too, is commonly given to the master for teaching him his trade. They who cannot give money, give time, or become bound for more than the usual number of years; a consideration which, though it is not always advantageous to the master, on account of the usual idleness of apprentices, is always disadvantageous to the apprentice. In country labour, on the contrary, the labourer, while he is employed about the easier, learns the more difficult parts of his business, and his own labour maintains him through all the different stages of his employment. It is reasonable, therefore, that in Europe the wages of mechanics, artificers, and manufacturers, should be somewhat higher than those of common labourers. They are so accordingly, and their superior gains make them, in most places, be considered as a superior rank of people. This superiority, however, is generally very small: the daily or weekly earnings of journeymen in the more common sorts of manufactures, such as those of plain linen and woollen cloth, computed at an average, are, in most places, very little more than the day-wages of common labourers. Their employment, indeed, is more steady and uniform, and the superiority of their earnings, taking the whole year together, may be somewhat greater. It seems evidently, however, to be no greater than what is sufficient to compensate the superior expense of their education. Education in the ingenious arts, and in the liberal professions, is still more tedious and expensive. The pecuniary recompence, therefore, of painters and sculptors, of lawyers and physicians, ought to be much more liberal; and it is so accordingly.
p11.zh: 欧洲的政策将所有机械师、工匠和制造商的劳动视为熟练的劳动;而所有国家的劳工则视为我们共同的劳动。 它似乎认为前者的性格比后者的性格更优美,更微妙. 也许在某些情况下是这样;但大部分情况并非如此,因为我将努力逐一进行。 因此,欧洲的法律和惯例规定,为了使任何人有资格从事一种劳动,必须进行学徒培训,尽管在不同的地方有不同程度的严格程度。 他们让另一个人自由,对每个身体开放。 在继续学徒期间,学徒的全部劳动属于他的主人. 与此同时,在许多情况下,他必须被父母或关系所维持,而且几乎在所有情况下,都必须由父母或关系所包扎。 一些钱,也常赠与主人,以教导他从事贸易. 那些不能给钱、时间或约束时间超过通常年数的人;这种考虑虽然并不总是对主人有利,但由于学徒们通常闲置,但总是对学徒们不利。 相反,在乡下劳动中,工人们虽然受雇于比较容易的人,却学习了自己企业中比较困难的部分,他自己劳动维持他贯穿他就业的所有不同阶段. 因此,在欧洲,机械师、工艺师和制造商的工资应该比普通工人的工资高一些是合理的。 他们因此如此,他们的优越收益使他们,在大多数地方,都被视为一个优越的人物. 然而,这种优越性一般很小:在较常见的制造业中,例如普通麻布和羊毛布的日常或每周收入,平均计算,在大多数地方都比普通工人的日薪少得多。 她们的就业确实更加稳定、统一,她们收入的优越性,使整个一年合在一起,可能更大一些。 然而,显然,这不会超过足以补偿其教育费用的数额。天才艺术教育,自由职业教育,仍然比较乏味,昂贵. 因此,画家和雕塑家、律师和医生的金钱补偿应该更加宽松;因此,这种补偿应该更加宽松。

p12.original: The profits of stock seem to be very little affected by the easiness or difficulty of learning the trade in which it is employed. All the different ways in which stock is commonly employed in great towns seem, in reality, to be almost equally easy and equally difficult to learn. One branch, either of foreign or domestic trade, cannot well be a much more intricate business than another.
p12.zh: 股票的利润似乎很少受到容易或难以了解其所从事贸易的影响。 在大城市中普遍使用股票的所有不同方式实际上似乎几乎同样容易和同样难学。 一个分支,无论是对外贸易还是国内贸易,都不可能比另一个分支复杂得多。

p13.original: Thirdly, the wages of labour in different occupations vary with the constancy or inconstancy of employment.
p13.zh: 第三,不同职业的劳动工资随就业的耐性或不耐性而变化。

p14.original: Employment is much more constant in some trades than in others. In the greater part of manufactures, a journeyman maybe pretty sure of employment almost every day in the year that he is able to work. A mason or bricklayer, on the contrary, can work neither in hard frost nor in foul weather, and his employment at all other times depends upon the occasional calls of his customers. He is liable, in consequence, to be frequently without any. What he earns, therefore, while he is employed, must not only maintain him while he is idle, but make him some compensation for those anxious and desponding moments which the thought of so precarious a situation must sometimes occasion. Where the computed earnings of the greater part of manufacturers, accordingly, are nearly upon a level with the day-wages of common labourers, those of masons and bricklayers are generally from one-half more to double those wages. Where common labourers earn four or five shillings a-week, masons and bricklayers frequently earn seven and eight; where the former earn six, the latter often earn nine and ten; and where the former earn nine and ten, as in London, the latter commonly earn fifteen and eighteen. No species of skilled labour, however, seems more easy to learn than that of masons and bricklayers. Chairmen in London, during the summer season, are said sometimes to be employed as bricklayers. The high wages of those workmen, therefore, are not so much the recompence of their skill, as the compensation for the inconstancy of their employment.
p14.zh: 有些行业的就业比其他行业的就业稳定得多。 在大部分的制造中, 一个旅行者也许相当确定 他几乎每天工作,当他能够工作。 相反,一个泥瓦匠或砖匠既不能在严霜中工作,也不能在恶劣的天气中工作,他在其他所有时间的就业都取决于他的顾客偶尔的呼唤. 因此,他有责任经常不带任何东西。 因此,他在工作期间所得的收入,不仅必须维持他在闲暇期间的生计,而且必须使这些焦虑和沮丧的时刻得到一些补偿,而这种时刻有时必须想到这种不稳定的局面。 因此,如果大部分制造商的计算收入与普通工人的日薪接近水平,那么砖匠和砖匠的日薪一般从工资的半数增加到两倍。普通工人每周挣四、五先令,砖匠和砖匠往往挣七、八先令;前者赚六先令,后者赚九、十先令;前者赚九、十先令,如伦敦,后者通常赚十五、十八先令。 然而,似乎没有哪一种技术工人比泥瓦匠和砖匠更容易学习。在伦敦的主席,在夏季,据说有时被雇用为砖匠。 因此,这些工人的高工资与其说是技能的回报,不如说是工作不便的补偿。

p15.original: A house-carpenter seems to exercise rather a nicer and a more ingenious trade than a mason. In most places, however, for it is not universally so, his day-wages are somewhat lower. His employment, though it depends much, does not depend so entirely upon the occasional calls of his customers; and it is not liable to be interrupted by the weather.
p15.zh: 家用木匠似乎锻炼得比泥瓦匠更优雅,更巧妙的买卖. 然而,在大多数地方,由于并非普遍如此,他的日薪略低。 他的工作虽然在很大程度上取决于他的工作,但并不完全取决于他的客户偶尔的电话;而且不会因天气而中断。

p16.original: When the trades which generally afford constant employment, happen in a particular place not to do so, the wages of the workmen always rise a good deal above their ordinary proportion to those of common labour. In London, almost all journeymen artificers are liable to be called upon and dismissed by their masters from day to day, and from week to week, in the same manner as day-labourers in other places. The lowest order of artificers, journeymen tailors, accordingly, earn their half-a-crown a-day, though eighteen pence may be reckoned the wages of common labour. In small towns and country villages, the wages of journeymen tailors frequently scarce equal those of common labour; but in London they are often many weeks without employment, particularly during the summer.
p16.zh: 当一般能够持续就业的行业在某一地点发生时,工人的工资总是比普通工人的工资高出很多。在伦敦,几乎所有的游人工匠都可能与其他地方的日工一样,在日间和周间受到主人的召唤和解雇.艺术家、旅行者裁缝的最低等级因此每天挣到一半,尽管18便士可以算作普通劳工的工资。 在小城镇和乡村村庄,旅行者的工资往往很少与普通劳动力的工资相等;但在伦敦,他们往往有许多周没有工作,特别是在夏季。

p17.original: When the inconstancy of employment is combined with the hardship, disagreeableness, and dirtiness of the work, it sometimes raises the wages of the most common labour above those of the most skilful artificers. A collier working by the piece is supposed, at Newcastle, to earn commonly about double, and, in many parts of Scotland, about three times, the wages of common labour. His high wages arise altogether from the hardship, disagreeableness, and dirtiness of his work. His employment may, upon most occasions, be as constant as he pleases. The coal-heavers in London exercise a trade which, in hardship, dirtiness, and disagreeableness, almost equals that of colliers; and, from the unavoidable irregularity in the arrivals of coal-ships, the employment of the greater part of them is necessarily very inconstant. If colliers, therefore, commonly earn double and triple the wages of common labour, it ought not to seem unreasonable that coal-heavers should sometimes earn four and five times those wages. In the inquiry made into their condition a few years ago, it was found that, at the rate at which they were then paid, they could earn from six to ten shillings a-day. Six shillings are about four times the wages of common labour in London; and, in every particular trade, the lowest common earnings may always be considered as those of the far greater number. How extravagant soever those earnings may appear, if they were more than sufficient to compensate all the disagreeable circumstances of the business, there would soon be so great a number of competitors, as, in a trade which has no exclusive privilege, would quickly reduce them to a lower rate.
p17.zh: 当就业不稳与工作艰苦、不愉快和肮脏结合起来时,有时会提高最普通工人的工资,高于最熟练的工匠的工资。 在纽卡斯尔,一个从事该作品的钳工应该能普遍挣到两倍左右的收入,在苏格兰的许多地方,大约是3倍的普通劳动工资. 他的高工资完全源于他工作的艰苦、不愉快和肮脏。在大多数情况下,他的工作可能保持不变。伦敦的煤矿工人从事一种贸易,这种贸易在艰苦、肮脏和不愉快的情况下几乎等同于煤矿工人;而且,由于煤矿船的到来必然出现不规则的情况,他们中大部分人的就业必然是不稳定的。 因此,如果煤矿工人通常挣得的普通劳动工资的两倍和三倍,那么有时煤矿工人挣得的工资是普通劳动工资的四倍和五倍,这不应该是不合理的。 在几年前对他们的情况进行调查时发现,按照他们当时的付款率,他们每天可以挣到六至十先令。 六先令是伦敦普通劳工工资的四倍左右;在每一个特定行业中,共同收入最低者可始终被认为是数量大得多者。不论这些收入如何奢侈,如果它们足以补偿企业的所有不祥情况,那么,很快就会有如此众多的竞争者,因为在没有专属特权的贸易中,这些竞争者会很快降低到较低的利率。

p18.original: The constancy or inconstancy of employment cannot affect the ordinary profits of stock in any particular trade. Whether the stock is or is not constantly employed, depends, not upon the trade, but the trader.
p18.zh: 就业的停滞或不稳不影响任何特定行业股票的普通利润。股票是否持续使用,取决于,不是贸易,而是贸易商。

p19.original: Fourthly, the wages of labour vary according to the small or great trust which must be reposed in the workmen.
p19.zh: 第四,劳动工资因工人必须背负的微小或巨大信任而不同。

p20.original: The wages of goldsmiths and jewellers are everywhere superior to those of many other workmen, not only of equal, but of much superior ingenuity, on account of the precious materials with which they are entrusted. We trust our health to the physician, our fortune, and sometimes our life and reputation, to the lawyer and attorney. Such confidence could not safely be reposed in people of a very mean or low condition. Their reward must be such, therefore, as may give them that rank in the society which so important a trust requires. The long time and the great expense which must be laid out in their education, when combined with this circumstance, necessarily enhance still further the price of their labour.
p20.zh: 金匠和珠宝商的工资在各地都优于许多其他工人的工资,不仅平等,而且由于受委托的珍贵材料,具有相当高的智慧. 我们相信我们的健康 依靠医生, 我们的财富, 有时我们的生活和名誉, 和律师和律师。 这种信心不能安全地重置在条件极差或低的人身上。 因此,他们的奖励必须是给予他们在社会中如此重要、需要信任的级别。 如果加上这种情况,教育中必须规定的长期和巨大开支必然会进一步提高其劳动的代价。

p21.original: When a person employs only his own stock in trade, there is no trust; and the credit which he may get from other people, depends, not upon the nature of the trade, but upon their opinion of his fortune, probity and prudence. The different rates of profit, therefore, in the different branches of trade, cannot arise from the different degrees of trust reposed in the traders.
p21.zh: 当一个人只雇用自己的股票从事贸易时,就没有信任;他可以从其他人那里得到的信用,不取决于贸易的性质,而是取决于他们对他财富、正直和谨慎的看法。 因此,不同贸易分支的不同利润率不能产生于对贸易商的不同程度的信任。

p22.original: Fifthly, the wages of labour in different employments vary according to the probability or improbability of success in them.
p22.zh: 第五,不同行业的劳动工资因成功概率或不可能不同而不同。

p23.original: The probability that any particular person shall ever be qualified for the employments to which he is educated, is very different in different occupations. In the greatest part of mechanic trades success is almost certain; but very uncertain in the liberal professions. Put your son apprentice to a shoemaker, there is little doubt of his learning to make a pair of shoes; but send him to study the law, it as at least twenty to one if he ever makes such proficiency as will enable him to live by the business. In a perfectly fair lottery, those who draw the prizes ought to gain all that is lost by those who draw the blanks. In a profession, where twenty fail for one that succeeds, that one ought to gain all that should have been gained by the unsuccessful twenty. The counsellor at law, who, perhaps, at near forty years of age, begins to make something by his profession, ought to receive the retribution, not only of his own so tedious and expensive education, but of that of more than twenty others, who are never likely to make any thing by it. How extravagant soever the fees of counsellors at law may sometimes appear, their real retribution is never equal to this. Compute, in any particular place, what is likely to be annually gained, and what is likely to be annually spent, by all the different workmen in any common trade, such as that of shoemakers or weavers, and you will find that the former sum will generally exceed the latter. But make the same computation with regard to all the counsellors and students of law, in all the different Inns of Court, and you will find that their annual gains bear but a very small proportion to their annual expense, even though you rate the former as high, and the latter as low, as can well be done. The lottery of the law, therefore, is very far from being a perfectly fair lottery; and that as well as many other liberal and honourable professions, is, in point of pecuniary gain, evidently under-recompensed.
p23.zh: 任何特定的人都有资格从事其所受教育的职业,这种可能性在不同的职业中有很大不同。 在机械师行业的最大部分几乎是肯定的;但在自由职业中却非常不确定.将你儿子的徒弟交给一个鞋匠,他学制一双鞋是没有什么疑问的;但让他去学习法律,至少是20到1个,如果他有这种能力,使他能靠这个生意生活. 在完全公平的彩票中,那些抽奖的人应该获得那些抽空的人所损失的一切.在一个职业中,如果有20名失败者失败了,那就应该从20名失败者那里获得所有应得的利益。律师,也许,在将近40岁的时候,开始根据自己的职业做一些事情,他应该得到报应,不仅因为他自己如此乏味和昂贵的教育,而且因为另外20多人的教育,他们永远不可能通过这种教育做任何事情。 无论律师费多么奢侈,他们真正的报复行为有时都可能显得如此,这绝不是相等的。 在任何特定地点计算任何普通行业的所有不同工人,如鞋匠或织工每年可能获得的和每年可能花费的金额,你会发现,前一笔金额一般会超过后者。 但对所有律师和学生都做同样的计算, 在法院的所有不同学院里,你会发现他们的年收益 只占他们年支出的很小一部分, 即使你把前者评为高, 而后者评为低, 做得很好。 因此,法律的彩票远非完全公平的彩票;而且,与许多其他自由而光荣的职业一样,以金钱收益为标准,显然报酬不足。

p24.original: Those professions keep their level, however, with other occupations; and, notwithstanding these discouragements, all the most generous and liberal spirits are eager to crowd into them. Two different causes contribute to recommend them. First, the desire of the reputation which attends upon superior excellence in any of them; and, secondly, the natural confidence which every man has, more or less, not only in his own abilities, but in his own good fortune.
p24.zh: 然而,这些职业与其他职业一样保持其水平;而且,尽管有这些挫折,所有最慷慨和最自由的精神都热切地希望加入这些职业。 两个不同的原因有助于推荐它们。 首先,任何一种事物中,声望都以优异的品格为重;其次,每个人的自然信心,无论多寡,不仅在自身能力上,而且在自身好运气上,都是如此。

p25.original: To excel in any profession, in which but few arrive at mediocrity, it is the most decisive mark of what is called genius, or superior talents. The public admiration which attends upon such distinguished abilities makes always a part of their reward; a greater or smaller, in proportion as it is higher or lower in degree. It makes a considerable part of that reward in the profession of physic; a still greater, perhaps, in that of law; in poetry and philosophy it makes almost the whole.
p25.zh: 在任何职业中都表现优异,在这种职业中,很少有人达到平庸的地步,这是所谓天才或优秀才华的最决定性的标志。公众对这种杰出能力的钦佩始终是奖励的一部分;无论大小,视其程度高低的比例而定。 在物理学专业中,它成为这一奖励的相当一部分;在法律专业中,它或许是更大的;在诗歌和哲学领域,它几乎是整体。

p26.original: There are some very agreeable and beautiful talents, of which the possession commands a certain sort of admiration, but of which the exercise, for the sake of gain, is considered, whether from reason or prejudice, as a sort of public prostitution. The pecuniary recompence, therefore, of those who exercise them in this manner, must be sufficient, not only to pay for the time, labour, and expense of acquiring the talents, but for the discredit which attends the employment of them as the means of subsistence. The exorbitant rewards of players, opera-singers, opera-dancers, etc. are founded upon those two principles; the rarity and beauty of the talents, and the discredit of employing them in this manner. It seems absurd at first sight, that we should despise their persons, and yet reward their talents with the most profuse liberality. While we do the one, however, we must of necessity do the other, Should the public opinion or prejudice ever alter with regard to such occupations, their pecuniary recompence would quickly diminish. More people would apply to them, and the competition would quickly reduce the price of their labour. Such talents, though far from being common, are by no means so rare as imagined. Many people possess them in great perfection, who disdain to make this use of them; and many more are capable of acquiring them, if any thing could be made honourably by them.
p26.zh: 有一些非常受人欢迎和美丽的才华,其中占有者赢得了某种钦佩,但为了获得利益,无论出于理由还是出于偏见,这种锻炼都被认为是一种公共卖淫。 因此,以这种方式行使权力的人的金钱补偿必须足够,不仅支付时间、劳动和获得人才的费用,而且支付雇用他们作为生计手段的名誉损失。玩家、歌剧歌手、歌剧舞者等的巨额奖励都基于这两项原则;人才的稀有和美丽,以及以这种方式雇用人才的失信。 我们轻视他们的人格,却以最慷慨的自由主义来奖励他们的才能,这乍一看似乎是荒谬的。 然而,尽管我们这样做,但我们必须这样做,如果公众舆论或偏见改变这种职业,他们的金钱补偿将迅速减少。更多的人会申请给他们,竞争会很快降低他们的劳动价格. 这种才华虽然远非常见,但绝非想象中如此罕见.许多人拥有这些财富,他们不屑于利用这些财富;还有许多人有能力获得这些财富,如果他们能以荣誉为荣的话。

p27.original: The over-weening conceit which the greater part of men have of their own abilities, is an ancient evil remarked by the philosophers and moralists of all ages. Their absurd presumption in their own good fortune has been less taken notice of. It is, however, if possible, still more universal. There is no man living, who, when in tolerable health and spirits, has not some share of it. The chance of gain is by every man more or less over-valued, and the chance of loss is by most men under-valued, and by scarce any man, who is in tolerable health and spirits, valued more than it is worth.
p27.zh: 大部分人有本领的过度自以为是,这是各年龄的哲学家和道德主义者所言的古老的罪恶。 他们自己幸运的荒谬假设却很少被注意到。 然而,如果可能,它仍然更加具有普遍性。没有任何人活着,当他身体和精神处于可容忍的状态时,他没有获得其中的一部分。获得的几率是每个男人或多或少地被高估,而损失的几率是大多数男人低估的价值,而任何一个男人,在可容忍的健康和精神中,价值都比价值高。

p28.original: That the chance of gain is naturally overvalued, we may learn from the universal success of lotteries. The world neither ever saw, nor ever will see, a perfectly fair lottery, or one in which the whole gain compensated the whole loss; because the undertaker could make nothing by it. In the state lotteries, the tickets are really not worth the price which is paid by the original subscribers, and yet commonly sell in the market for twenty, thirty, and sometimes forty per cent. advance. The vain hopes of gaining some of the great prizes is the sole cause of this demand. The soberest people scarce look upon it as a folly to pay a small sum for the chance of gaining ten or twenty thousand pounds, though they know that even that small sum is perhaps twenty or thirty per cent. more than the chance is worth. In a lottery in which no prize exceeded twenty pounds, though in other respects it approached much nearer to a perfectly fair one than the common state lotteries, there would not be the same demand for tickets. In order to have a better chance for some of the great prizes, some people purchase several tickets; and others, small shares in a still greater number. There is not, however, a more certain proposition in mathematics, than that the more tickets you adventure upon, the more likely you are to be a loser. Adventure upon all the tickets in the lottery, and you lose for certain; and the greater the number of your tickets, the nearer you approach to this certainty.
p28.zh: 收益的机会自然被高估,我们可以从彩票的普遍成功中吸取教训。 世界从来没有看到,也永远不会看到一个完全公平的彩票,或者一个整个收益补偿了全部损失的彩票;因为承业者不能靠彩票作任何贡献。 在州彩票中,票价实际上不值原订户所付的价格,但通常在市场上售价为20%、30%,有时是40%。获得一些大奖的徒劳希望是这一需求的唯一原因。 最不清醒的人认为,为了获得一万或二万英镑的机会而支付一笔小款额是愚蠢的,尽管他们知道,即使这一小款额也许也只有20%或30%,比这一机会更有价值。 在一次没有奖金超过20磅的彩票中,虽然在其他方面,它比普通的州彩票更接近一个完全公平的彩票,但是对票价的要求却不同。 为了让一些大奖获得更好的机会,有些人购买了几张门票;而其他人则以更小的股价购买了几张门票. 然而,数学方面没有比这更确定的建议了, 你冒险的门票越多, 你就越有可能是个失败者。 在彩票上冒险,你必定亏损;你的彩票数量越多,你就越接近这种确定性。

p29.original: That the chance of loss is frequently undervalued, and scarce ever valued more than it is worth, we may learn from the very moderate profit of insurers. In order to make insurance, either from fire or sea-risk, a trade at all, the common premium must be sufficient to compensate the common losses, to pay the expense of management, and to afford such a profit as might have been drawn from an equal capital employed in any common trade. The person who pays no more than this, evidently pays no more than the real value of the risk, or the lowest price at which he can reasonably expect to insure it. But though many people have made a little money by insurance, very few have made a great fortune; and, from this consideration alone, it seems evident enough that the ordinary balance of profit and loss is not more advantageous in this than in other common trades, by which so many people make fortunes. Moderate, however, as the premium of insurance commonly is, many people despise the risk too much to care to pay it. Taking the whole kingdom at an average, nineteen houses in twenty, or rather, perhaps, ninety-nine in a hundred, are not insured from fire. Sea-risk is more alarming to the greater part of people; and the proportion of ships insured to those not insured is much greater. Many sail, however, at all seasons, and even in time of war, without any insurance. This may sometimes, perhaps, be done without any imprudence. When a great company, or even a great merchant, has twenty or thirty ships at sea, they may, as it were, insure one another. The premium saved up on them all may more than compensate such losses as they are likely to meet with in the common course of chances. The neglect of insurance upon shipping, however, in the same manner as upon houses, is, in most cases, the effect of no such nice calculation, but of mere thoughtless rashness, and presumptuous contempt of the risk.
p29.zh: 损失的机会往往被低估,而且价值从未超过价值,我们可以从保险公司的微小利润中吸取教训。 为了从火险或海上风险为贸易提供保险,共同保险费必须足以补偿共同损失,支付管理费用,并能够从任何共同贸易中雇用的同等资本中获得利润。支付不超过这一数额的人,显然支付不超过风险的实际价值,或他可以合理预期保险的最低价格。 但是,虽然许多人通过保险赚了一点钱,但很少有人赚了大钱;光是这一点,似乎就足够明显了,利润和损失的普通平衡在这方面并不比其他普通行业更有利,因为如此多的人通过这些行业赚钱. 然而,由于保险的保险费通常比较中度,许多人轻视这种风险而不愿支付。平均来说,整个王国有20个,或者说,100个,有99个房屋没有火险。 海险对大部分人来说更加令人震惊;被保险的船只与未投保船只的比例要高得多。 然而,许多船在所有的季节航行,甚至在战时,都没有保险。这样做有时也许不失为一种不失礼的做法。 当一个伟大的公司,甚至一个伟大的商人, 在海上有二三十艘船时, 他们可以像以前一样, 互相保险。所节省的保险费可能不止于补偿他们在共同的机会过程中可能遇到的损失。 然而,在大多数情况下,对航运的保险视而不见与对房屋的同样方式,并不是如此明智的计算,而只是轻率的轻率,以及自以为是地蔑视风险。

p30.original: The contempt of risk, and the presumptuous hope of success, are in no period of life more active than at the age at which young people choose their professions. How little the fear of misfortune is then capable of balancing the hope of good luck, appears still more evidently in the readiness of the common people to enlist as soldiers, or to go to sea, than in the eagerness of those of better fashion to enter into what are called the liberal professions.
p30.zh: 轻视风险和自以为是的成功希望,在一生中最活跃的莫过于年轻人选择职业的年龄。 那么,对不幸的恐惧如何能够平衡好运的希望,在普通民众是否愿意入伍或上海方面,比起那些更热衷于进入所谓自由职业的人,表现得更明显。

p31.original: What a common soldier may lose is obvious enough. Without regarding the danger, however, young volunteers never enlist so readily as at the beginning of a new war; and though they have scarce any chance of preferment, they figure to themselves, in their youthful fancies, a thousand occasions of acquiring honour and distinction which never occur. These romantic hopes make the whole price of their blood. Their pay is less than that of common labourers, and, in actual service, their fatigues are much greater.
p31.zh: 一个普通士兵可能失去的东西已经足够明显了。 然而,如果不考虑危险,青年志愿人员从未像在新战争开始时那样轻易入伍;尽管他们几乎没有任何偏好机会,但他们却在年轻时的幻想中认为,他们有千百次获得从未有过的荣誉和殊荣。 这些浪漫的希望 让他们的血液付出了一切代价 她们的工资低于普通工人,在实际服务中,她们的疲劳症要大得多。

p32.original: The lottery of the sea is not altogether so disadvantageous as that of the army. The son of a creditable labourer or artificer may frequently go to sea with his father's consent; but if he enlists as a soldier, it is always without it. Other people see some chance of his making something by the one trade; nobody but himself sees any of his making any thing by the other. The great admiral is less the object of public admiration than the great general; and the highest success in the sea service promises a less brilliant fortune and reputation than equal success in the land. The same difference runs through all the inferior degrees of preferment in both. By the rules of precedency, a captain in the navy ranks with a colonel in the army; but he does not rank with him in the common estimation. As the great prizes in the lottery are less, the smaller ones must be more numerous. Common sailors, therefore, more frequently get some fortune and preferment than common soldiers; and the hope of those prizes is what principally recommends the trade. Though their skill and dexterity are much superior to that of almost any artificers; and though their whole life is one continual scene of hardship and danger; yet for all this dexterity and skill, for all those hardships and dangers, while they remain in the condition of common sailors, they receive scarce any other recompence but the pleasure of exercising the one and of surmounting the other. Their wages are not greater than those of common labourers at the port which regulates the rate of seamen's wages. As they are continually going from port to port, the monthly pay of those who sail from all the different ports of Great Britain, is more nearly upon a level than that of any other workmen in those different places; and the rate of the port to and from which the greatest number sail, that is, the port of London, regulates that of all the rest. At London, the wages of the greater part of the different classes of workmen are about double those of the same classes at Edinburgh. But the sailors who sail from the port of London, seldom earn above three or four shillings a month more than those who sail from the port of Leith, and the difference is frequently not so great. In time of peace, and in the merchant-service, the London price is from a guinea to about seven-and-twenty shillings the calendar month. A common labourer in London, at the rate of nine or ten shillings a week, may earn in the calendar month from forty to five-and-forty shillings. The sailor, indeed, over and above his pay, is supplied with provisions. Their value, however, may not perhaps always exceed the difference between his pay and that of the common labourer; and though it sometimes should, the excess will not be clear gain to the sailor, because he cannot share it with his wife and family, whom he must maintain out of his wages at home.
p32.zh: 海上的彩票并不完全像军队的彩票那样不利。值得称道的劳工或工匠的儿子,经父亲同意,可以经常出海;但是,如果他作为士兵入伍,则总是没有这种机会。其他人看到他有某种机会用一种交易来制造东西;除了他自己,没有人看到他用另一种交易来制造任何东西。 大上将不如大将军为公众所钦佩;海务的最高成功保证了比在陆地上同等的成功要少的辉煌财富和名声.同样的差异贯穿了两者中所有低等偏好程度.依据先行规则,海军中有一名上尉在陆军中排队,但按照共同估计,他并不随军排队. 由于彩票中的大奖较少,所以小奖必须更多. 因此,与普通士兵相比,普通水手更经常地得到一些财富和偏好;而这些奖品的希望主要是推荐贸易。 虽然他们的技能和德行比几乎所有艺术家的要高得多;尽管他们一生都是不断的艰难和危险;然而,对于所有这些德行和技巧,尽管他们仍然处于普通水手的状态,但除了行使一种和超越另一种的乐趣之外,他们几乎没有任何其他补偿。 他们的工资不高于规定海员工资比例的港口普通工人的工资。 由于他们不断从港口到港口,从大不列颠所有不同港口航行的人的月薪比那些不同地方的任何其他工人的月薪要高得多;而人数最多的港口,即伦敦港,其往返率对所有其他港口的航行都作出了规定。在伦敦,不同阶层的工人中大部分的工资大约是爱丁堡同班工资的两倍. 但从伦敦港起航的水手们,每月的收入很少比从莱思港起航的水手多三四先令以上,这种差别往往不是那么大. 在和平时期,在商贸服务中,伦敦的价格从一个豚鼠到日历月的大约七先令和二十先令.伦敦的普通劳工,按每周9或10先令的费率计算,在日历月内可能挣得40至5和40先令.水手,实际上,除了工资之外,还有各种补给。 然而,他们的价值也许并不总是超过他和普通工人的工资差别;虽然有时应该如此,但多余的金额不会明显地为水手带来收益,因为他不能与妻子和家人分享,他必须用他家里的工资来维持这些妻子和家人。

p33.original: The dangers and hair-breadth escapes of a life of adventures, instead of disheartening young people, seem frequently to recommend a trade to them. A tender mother, among the inferior ranks of people, is often afraid to send her son to school at a sea-port town, lest the sight of the ships, and the conversation and adventures of the sailors, should entice him to go to sea. The distant prospect of hazards, from which we can hope to extricate ourselves by courage and address, is not disagreeable to us, and does not raise the wages of labour in any employment. It is otherwise with those in which courage and address can be of no avail. In trades which are known to be very unwholesome, the wages of labour are always remarkably high. Unwholesomeness is a species of disagreeableness, and its effects upon the wages of labour are to be ranked under that general head.
p33.zh: 冒险生活的危险和毛发包逃离,而不是令年轻人沮丧,似乎经常建议他们进行交易。温柔的母亲,在卑劣的人群中,常常害怕将儿子送到海港镇的学校,以免船只的目光,以及水手的谈话和冒险,引他上海.危险的遥远前景使我们希望通过勇气和解决而摆脱危险,我们对此并不感到不满,而且不会提高任何就业的劳动工资。 否则,勇气和发言毫无用处。 在众所周知非常不健全的行业中,劳动工资总是很高。 不完美是不容置疑的种类,其对劳动工资的影响要排在该总标题下.

p34.original: In all the different employments of stock, the ordinary rate of profit varies more or less with the certainty or uncertainty of the returns. These are, in general, less uncertain in the inland than in the foreign trade, and in some branches of foreign trade than in others; in the trade to North America, for example, than in that to Jamaica. The ordinary rate of profit always rises more or less with the risk. It does not, however, seem to rise in proportion to it, or so as to compensate it completely. Bankruptcies are most frequent in the most hazardous trades. The most hazardous of all trades, that of a smuggler, though, when the adventure succeeds, it is likewise the most profitable, is the infallible road to bankruptcy. The presumptuous hope of success seems to act here as upon all other occasions, and to entice so many adventurers into those hazardous trades, that their competition reduces the profit below what is sufficient to compensate the risk. To compensate it completely, the common returns ought, over and above the ordinary profits of stock, not only to make up for all occasional losses, but to afford a surplus profit to the adventurers, of the same nature with the profit of insurers. But if the common returns were sufficient for all this, bankruptcies would not be more frequent in these than in other trades.
p34.zh: 在股票的所有不同职业中,正常利润率随着收益的确定性或不确定性多少而变化。一般而言,内陆贸易的不确定性比对外贸易的不确定性要小,而外贸的某些分支贸易的不确定性比其他分支的不确定性小;例如,北美贸易的不确定性比牙买加的不确定性大。正常利润率总是随着风险多少增加而上升. 但是,它似乎没有按照它的比例增加,或者说是为了完全补偿它。 在最危险的行业中,破产最为常见。 在所有的行业中,最危险的是走私者,不过,当冒险成功时,它同样也是最有利可图的,是通往破产的不败之路。成功的先发制人希望似乎与所有其他场合一样在这里发挥作用,并吸引了这么多冒险者从事这些危险行业,以致他们的竞争将利润降低到足以补偿风险的水平以下。 为了完全补偿,除了股票的普通利润之外,共同收益不仅应弥补所有偶发损失,还应向冒险者提供与保险人利润性质相同的利润。 但是,如果共同收益足以应付所有这些情况,破产在这些行业中不会比其他行业更频繁。

p35.original: Of the five circumstances, therefore, which vary the wages of labour, two only affect the profits of stock; the agreeableness or disagreeableness of the business, and the risk or security with which it is attended. In point of agreeableness or disagreeableness, there is little or no difference in the far greater part of the different employments of stock, but a great deal in those of labour; and the ordinary profit of stock, though it rises with the risk, does not always seem to rise in proportion to it. It should follow from all this, that, in the same society or neighbourhood, the average and ordinary rates of profit in the different employments of stock should be more nearly upon a level than the pecuniary wages of the different sorts of labour.
p35.zh: 因此,在改变劳动工资的五种情况下,有两种情况只影响股票利润;企业的可接受性或可不同意性,以及企业承担的风险或担保。 从同意或不同意的角度来看,不同股票就业的绝大部分差别很小或没有,但劳动的差别很大;股票的普通利润虽然随着风险而上升,但似乎并不总是按其比例上升.由此,在同一社会或邻里,不同股票行业的平均和普通利润率应比不同种类劳动力的金钱工资更接近水平。

p36.original: They are so accordingly. The difference between the earnings of a common labourer and those of a well employed lawyer or physician, is evidently much greater than that between the ordinary profits in any two different branches of trade. The apparent difference, besides, in the profits of different trades, is generally a deception arising from our not always distinguishing what ought to be considered as wages, from what ought to be considered as profit.
p36.zh: 他们就是这样。普通工人的收入与受雇律师或医生的收入之间的差别,显然大大大于任何两个不同行业的普通利润之间的差别。 除了不同行业利润的明显差别外,我们通常不总是区分什么是工资,什么是利润。

p37.original: Apothecaries' profit is become a bye-word, denoting something uncommonly extravagant. This great apparent profit, however, is frequently no more than the reasonable wages of labour. The skill of an apothecary is a much nicer and more delicate matter than that of any artificer whatever; and the trust which is reposed in him is of much greater importance. He is the physician of the poor in all cases, and of the rich when the distress or danger is not very great. His reward, therefore, ought to be suitable to his skill and his trust; and it arises generally from the price at which he sells his drugs. But the whole drugs which the best employed apothecary in a large market-town, will sell in a year, may not perhaps cost him above thirty or forty pounds. Though he should sell them, therefore, for three or four hundred, or at a thousand per cent. profit, this may frequently be no more than the reasonable wages of his labour, charged, in the only way in which he can charge them, upon the price of his drugs. The greater part of the apparent profit is real wages disguised in the garb of profit.
p37.zh: 药剂师的利润变成了一个拜词, 指一些不寻常的奢侈品。 然而,这种明显的巨大利润往往不超过合理的劳动工资。药剂师的技巧比任何艺术家的技巧要好得多,更微妙;对他的信任要重要得多。 他在所有情况下都是穷人的医生,在危难或危险不大时,他是富人的医生。 因此,他的奖赏应该适合他的技能和信任;这一般来自他出售毒品的价格。 但是,在大型市场集市中最优秀的药剂师 一年后就会卖掉的毒品 可能不会超过三四十磅 因此,尽管他应该出售三、四百份,或以千分百的价格出售,但利润往往不超过他按药物价格收取的合理工资。利润的较大部分是伪装成利润的实际工资。

p38.original: In a small sea-port town, a little grocer will make forty or fifty per cent. upon a stock of a single hundred pounds, while a considerable wholesale merchant in the same place will scarce make eight or ten per cent. upon a stock of ten thousand. The trade of the grocer may be necessary for the conveniency of the inhabitants, and the narrowness of the market may not admit the employment of a larger capital in the business. The man, however, must not only live by his trade, but live by it suitably to the qualifications which it requires. Besides possessing a little capital, he must be able to read, write, and account and must be a tolerable judge, too, of perhaps fifty or sixty different sorts of goods, their prices, qualities, and the markets where they are to be had cheapest. He must have all the knowledge, in short, that is necessary for a great merchant, which nothing hinders him from becoming but the want of a sufficient capital. Thirty or forty pounds a year cannot be considered as too great a recompence for the labour of a person so accomplished. Deduct this from the seemingly great profits of his capital, and little more will remain, perhaps, than the ordinary profits of stock. The greater part of the apparent profit is, in this case too, real wages.
p38.zh: 在一个海港小镇,一个小杂货店将达到百分之四十或百分之五十. 在一个一百磅的股票上,一个相当大数量的批发商在同一地方将很少达到百分之八或百分之十. 在一个一万磅的股票上,一个小杂货店将达到百分之四十或百分之五十.杂货商的贸易对于居民的容留可能是必要的,市场狭窄可能不允许在企业中雇用更大的资本. 然而,此人不仅必须靠他的行业生活,而且必须靠这种行业过着符合其所需资格的生活。 除了拥有一点资本之外,他还必须能够读、写和记账,并且必须能够成为可能包括50或60种不同商品、其价格、品质和最廉价的市场在内的可容忍的法官。 他必须拥有一切知识,简言之,对于一个大商人来说,这是必要的,这没有什么妨碍他成为只有足够资本的匮乏.一年三四十磅不能被认为是对如此成就的人的劳动的过度补偿. 从他资本的看来巨大的利润中扣除这一点,也许剩下的可能比普通的股票利润要少得多。 在这种情况下,利润的较大部分是实际工资。

p39.original: The difference between the apparent profit of the retail and that of the wholesale trade, is much less in the capital than in small towns and country villages. Where ten thousand pounds can be employed in the grocery trade, the wages of the grocer's labour must be a very trifling addition to the real profits of so great a stock. The apparent profits of the wealthy retailer, therefore, are there more nearly upon a level with those of the wholesale merchant. It is upon this account that goods sold by retail are generally as cheap, and frequently much cheaper, in the capital than in small towns and country villages. Grocery goods, for example, are generally much cheaper; bread and butchers' meat frequently as cheap. It costs no more to bring grocery goods to the great town than to the country village; but it costs a great deal more to bring corn and cattle, as the greater part of them must be brought from a much greater distance. The prime cost of grocery goods, therefore, being the same in both places, they are cheapest where the least profit is charged upon them. The prime cost of bread and butchers' meat is greater in the great town than in the country village; and though the profit is less, therefore they are not always cheaper there, but often equally cheap. In such articles as bread and butchers' meat, the same cause which diminishes apparent profit, increases prime cost. The extent of the market, by giving employment to greater stocks, diminishes apparent profit; but by requiring supplies from a greater distance, it increases prime cost. This diminution of the one and increase of the other, seem, in most cases, nearly to counterbalance one another; which is probably the reason that, though the prices of corn and cattle are commonly very different in different parts of the kingdom, those of bread and butchers' meat are generally very nearly the same through the greater part of it.
p39.zh: 零售业的表面利润与批发业的利润之间的差别,在首都比在小城镇和乡村小的要小得多. 在杂货店可以雇用一万英镑的地方,杂货店工人的工资必须比如此庞大的股票的实际利润少得多。 因此,富裕零售商的利润与批发商的利润接近。零售销售的商品一般在首都比在小城镇和乡村便宜得多。 例如,杂货一般便宜得多;面包和屠夫的肉往往便宜很多。 把杂货带到这个大城市比到乡村村要花很多钱;但把玉米和牛带到那里要花很多钱,因为大部分玉米和牛必须从很远的距离运过来。 因此,杂货品的主要成本在两个地方都是一样的,在收取最低利润的地方,价格最便宜。面包和屠夫的肉类价格在大镇比乡下村要高;虽然利润较少,但因此在乡下并不总是便宜,但往往同样便宜. 在面包和屠夫的肉类等物品中,同样减少表面利润的事业也增加了主要成本。市场的规模,通过向更多的股票提供就业机会,减少了明显的利润;但是,由于需要更远的供给,它增加了基本成本。一种的缩减和另一种的增加,在多数情况下似乎几乎相互抵消;这可能是由于这个原因,虽然在王国的不同地方,玉米和牛的价格通常有很大不同,但面包和屠夫的肉的价格一般通过它的大部分而几乎相同。

p40.original: Though the profits of stock, both in the wholesale and retail trade, are generally less in the capital than in small towns and country villages, yet great fortunes are frequently acquired from small beginnings in the former, and scarce ever in the latter. In small towns and country villages, on account of the narrowness of the market, trade cannot always be extended as stock extends. In such places, therefore, though the rate of a particular person's profits may be very high, the sum or amount of them can never be very great, nor consequently that of his annual accumulation. In great towns, on the contrary, trade can be extended as stock increases, and the credit of a frugal and thriving man increases much faster than his stock. His trade is extended in proportion to the amount of both; and the sum or amount of his profits is in proportion to the extent of his trade, and his annual accumulation in proportion to the amount of his profits. It seldom happens, however, that great fortunes are made, even in great towns, by any one regular, established, and well-known branch of business, but in consequence of a long life of industry, frugality, and attention. Sudden fortunes, indeed, are sometimes made in such places, by what is called the trade of speculation. The speculative merchant exercises no one regular, established, or well-known branch of business. He is a corn merchant this year, and a wine merchant the next, and a sugar, tobacco, or tea merchant the year after. He enters into every trade, when he foresees that it is likely to lie more than commonly profitable, and he quits it when he foresees that its profits are likely to return to the level of other trades. His profits and losses, therefore, can bear no regular proportion to those of any one established and well-known branch of business. A bold adventurer may sometimes acquire a considerable fortune by two or three successful speculations, but is just as likely to lose one by two or three unsuccessful ones. This trade can be carried on nowhere but in great towns. It is only in places of the most extensive commerce and correspondence that the intelligence requisite for it can be had.
p40.zh: 虽然在批发和零售贸易中,股票的利润在首都一般少于小城镇和乡村,但财富往往从前者的小规模开始获得,而在后者则很少。 在小城镇和乡村,由于市场狭窄,贸易不能总是随着股票的扩展而扩展。 因此,在这种地方,虽然某一个人的利润率可能很高,但利润的总额或数额永远不可能很大,因此也不可能是每年积累的利润。 相反,在大城市,随着股票的增加,贸易可以扩展,一个节俭和繁荣的人的信用增长比他的股票快得多。其贸易量按两者的金额比例予以扩大;其利润的总额或金额按其贸易量比例予以扩大,其年积累量按其利润比例予以扩大. 然而,即使是在大城市,也很少出现由任何一家正规的、有名的、有名的工商业分支创造巨大财富的情况,但这种财富是工业、节俭和关注的长寿的结果。 的确,突然的财富有时是在这种地方,通过所谓的投机交易来创造的。投机商不从事任何正常、固定或知名的商业活动。 他今年是玉米商 下一年是葡萄酒商 下一年是糖、烟草或茶叶商 他进入了每一个行业,当他预见到这种行业可能比通常的利润更有利可图时,他退出了这种行业,当他预见到其利润有可能恢复到其他行业的水平时。 因此,他的利润和损失不能与任何已设立和众所周知的工商分支的利润和损失成正比。大胆的冒险家有时可能通过两三次成功的猜测获得可观的财富,但同样有可能以两三次失败的猜测失去一对. 这种贸易除了在大城市里是无处可去的。只有在最广泛的商业和通信场所,才能拥有必要的情报。

p41.original: The five circumstances above mentioned, though they occasion considerable inequalities in the wages of labour and profits of stock, occasion none in the whole of the advantages and disadvantages, real or imaginary, of the different employments of either. The nature of those circumstances is such, that they make up for a small pecuniary gain in some, and counterbalance a great one in others.
p41.zh: 上述五种情况虽然在劳动工资和股票利润方面造成了相当大的不平等,但两者中任何一种都不存在实际或想象的不同就业的利弊。这些情况的性质如此之大,以致于它们弥补了某些情况下的小额金钱收益,而抵消了另一些情况下的巨额利润。

p42.original: In order, however, that this equality may take place in the whole of their advantages or disadvantages, three things are requisite, even where there is the most perfect freedom. First the employments must be well known and long established in the neighbourhood; secondly, they must be in their ordinary, or what may be called their natural state; and, thirdly, they must be the sole or principal employments of those who occupy them.
p42.zh: 然而,为了实现这种平等,无论是在他们的优势还是劣势方面,必须具备三项条件,即使有最完美的自由。 首先,就业必须是众所周知的,而且长期在邻里建立;其次,就业必须是普通的,或者可以说是其自然状态;第三,就业必须是占据就业者的唯一或主要就业。

p43.original: First, This equality can take place only in those employments which are well known, and have been long established in the neighbourhood.
p43.zh: 第一,这种平等只能发生在那些众所周知、而且长期在邻里建立的职业中。

p44.original: Where all other circumstances are equal, wages are generally higher in new than in old trades. When a projector attempts to establish a new manufacture, he must at first entice his workmen from other employments, by higher wages than they can either earn in their own trades, or than the nature of his work would otherwise require; and a considerable time must pass away before he can venture to reduce them to the common level. Manufactures for which the demand arises altogether from fashion and fancy, are continually changing, and seldom last long enough to be considered as old established manufactures. Those, on the contrary, for which the demand arises chiefly from use or necessity, are less liable to change, and the same form or fabric may continue in demand for whole centuries together. The wages of labour, therefore, are likely to be higher in manufactures of the former, than in those of the latter kind. Birmingham deals chiefly in manufactures of the former kind; Sheffield in those of the latter; and the wages of labour in those two different places are said to be suitable to this difference in the nature of their manufactures.
p44.zh: 在所有其他情况都相同的情况下,新行业的工资一般高于旧行业的工资。 当投影员试图建立新制造时,他首先必须诱导他的工人离开其他职业,他们的工资要高于他们在自己的行业中挣得的工资,或者比他的工作性质需要的还要高;而且他必须经过相当长的时间才能冒险将其降低到共同的水平.需求完全来自时尚和花哨的制造不断在变化,而且很少持续足够长的时间被视为老旧的制成品。 相反,这些需求主要来自使用或必要性,因此较难改变,而且同样的形式或结构可能在整个世纪中继续需求。 因此,前者的制造业的劳动工资可能高于后者的制造业。伯明翰主要从事前一种制造;谢菲尔德从事后一种制造;这两个不同地点的劳动工资据说适合其制造性质的这种差别。

p45.original: The establishment of any new manufacture, of any new branch of commerce, or of any new practice in agriculture, is always a speculation from which the projector promises himself extraordinary profits. These profits sometimes are very great, and sometimes, more frequently, perhaps, they are quite otherwise; but, in general, they bear no regular proportion to those of other old trades in the neighbourhood. If the project succeeds, they are commonly at first very high. When the trade or practice becomes thoroughly established and well known, the competition reduces them to the level of other trades.
p45.zh: 任何新制造、任何新的商业分支或任何农业新做法的建立,总是一种投机行为,投影者从中许诺自己会获得超乎寻常的利润。 这些利润有时非常大,有时甚至更经常,也许不是那样的;但总的来说,它们与附近其他旧行业的利润没有固定比例。 如果项目成功,它们通常在一开始非常高。 当这种贸易或做法得到彻底确立和广为人知时,竞争就会将它们降低到其他贸易的水平。

p46.original: Secondly, this equality in the whole of the advantages and disadvantages of the different employments of labour and stock, can take place only in the ordinary, or what may be called the natural state of those employments.
p46.zh: 第二,劳动和库存不同就业的利弊整体上这种平等,只能发生在普通或所谓的这些就业的自然状态。

p47.original: The demand for almost every different species of labour is sometimes greater, and sometimes less than usual. In the one case, the advantages of the employment rise above, in the other they fall below the common level. The demand for country labour is greater at hay-time and harvest than during the greater part of the year; and wages rise with the demand. In time of war, when forty or fifty thousand sailors are forced from the merchant service into that of the king, the demand for sailors to merchant ships necessarily rises with their scarcity; and their wages, upon such occasions, commonly rise from a guinea and seven-and-twenty shillings to forty shilling's and three pounds a-month. In a decaying manufacture, on the contrary, many workmen, rather than quit their own trade, are contented with smaller wages than would otherwise be suitable to the nature of their employment.
p47.zh: 对几乎每个不同种类的劳动力的需求有时更大,有时比通常的要少. 在一种情况下,就业的好处高于其他情况,低于共同水平。 在干草时间和收成方面,对国家劳动力的需求比大半年要大;工资随需求而增加。 在战时,当四,五万水兵被迫从商役进入国王的役务时,对商船的水兵的需求必然会随着他们的稀缺而增加;在这种场合,他们的工资通常从一豚鼠和七,二十先令增加到每月四十先令和三磅. 相反,在日益衰败的制造业中,许多工人,而不是放弃自己的贸易,却满足于工资低于本来适合其就业性质的工资。

p48.original: The profits of stock vary with the price of the commodities in which it is employed. As the price of any commodity rises above the ordinary or average rate, the profits of at least some part of the stock that is employed in bringing it to market, rise above their proper level, and as it falls they sink below it. All commodities are more or less liable to variations of price, but some are much more so than others. In all commodities which are produced by human industry, the quantity of industry annually employed is necessarily regulated by the annual demand, in such a manner that the average annual produce may, as nearly as possible, be equal to the average annual consumption. In some employments, it has already been observed, the same quantity of industry will always produce the same, or very nearly the same quantity of commodities. In the linen or woollen manufactures, for example, the same number of hands will annually work up very nearly the same quantity of linen and woollen cloth. The variations in the market price of such commodities, therefore, can arise only from some accidental variation in the demand. A public mourning raises the price of black cloth. But as the demand for most sorts of plain linen and woollen cloth is pretty uniform, so is likewise the price. But there are other employments in which the same quantity of industry will not always produce the same quantity of commodities. The same quantity of industry, for example, will, in different years, produce very different quantities of corn, wine, hops, sugar tobacco, etc. The price of such commodities, therefore, varies not only with the variations of demand, but with the much greater and more frequent variations of quantity, and is consequently extremely fluctuating; but the profit of some of the dealers must necessarily fluctuate with the price of the commodities. The operations of the speculative merchant are principally employed about such commodities. He endeavours to buy them up when he foresees that their price is likely to rise, and to sell them when it is likely to fall.
p48.zh: 股票的利润随所使用商品的价格而变化。 随着任何商品的价格高于正常或平均利率,至少一部分股票用于将其上市的利润,高于其适当水平,当其下跌时,其利润会降至低于该水平。 所有商品都或多或少容易受到价格变化的影响,但有些商品比其他商品要多得多。 在人类工业生产的所有商品中,每年雇用的工业数量必然受年度需求管制,使年平均产量尽可能接近于年平均消费。在一些职业中,已经观察到,同样的工业数量将永远生产同样的商品,或者几乎是相同的商品数量。 例如,在亚麻或羊毛制品中,同样数量的手每年能用上几乎相同的亚麻和羊毛布。 因此,这种商品的市场价格的变化只能由需求的某些偶然变化引起。公众的哀悼提高了黑布的价格. 但是,由于对大多数种类的普通亚麻布和羊毛布的需求相当一致,同样价格也相当一致. 但是,还有其他一些行业,同样数量工业并不总是生产同样数量的商品。 例如,工业的同样数量在不同年份将生产非常不同的玉米,葡萄酒,跳跃,糖烟草等. 因此,这种商品的价格不仅随需求的变化而变化,而且随着数量的变化而变化更大和更频繁,因此波动极大;而且一些经销商的利润必然随商品价格而波动。投机商主要从事这种商品的业务。 他试图在预见到价格可能上涨时买下它们,并在价格可能下跌时卖掉它们。

p49.original: Thirdly, this equality in the whole of the advantages and disadvantages of the different employments of labour and stock, can take place only in such as are the sole or principal employments of those who occupy them.
p49.zh: 第三,在劳动和库存的不同就业中,这种平等在总体上是利弊的,只有在那些就业者的唯一或主要就业中才能实现。

p50.original: When a person derives his subsistence from one employment, which does not occupy the greater part of his time, in the intervals of his leisure he is often willing to work at another for less wages than would otherwise suit the nature of the employment.
p50.zh: 当一个人从一份工作中获得生计时(该工作并不占用他的大部分时间),在闲暇时间里,他往往愿意在另一份工作上工作,其工资低于工作性质。

p51.original: There still subsists, in many parts of Scotland, a set of people called cottars or cottagers, though they were more frequent some years ago than they are now. They are a sort of out-servants of the landlords and farmers. The usual reward which they receive from their master is a house, a small garden for pot-herbs, as much grass as will feed a cow, and, perhaps, an acre or two of bad arable land. When their master has occasion for their labour, he gives them, besides, two pecks of oatmeal a-week, worth about sixteen pence sterling. During a great part of the year, he has little or no occasion for their labour, and the cultivation of their own little possession is not sufficient to occupy the time which is left at their own disposal. When such occupiers were more numerous than they are at present, they are said to have been willing to give their spare time for a very small recompence to any body, and to have wrought for less wages than other labourers. In ancient times, they seem to have been common all over Europe. In countries ill cultivated, and worse inhabited, the greater part of landlords and farmers could not otherwise provide themselves with the extraordinary number of hands which country labour requires at certain seasons. The daily or weekly recompence which such labourers occasionally received from their masters, was evidently not the whole price of their labour. Their small tenement made a considerable part of it. This daily or weekly recompence, however, seems to have been considered as the whole of it, by many writers who have collected the prices of labour and provisions in ancient times, and who have taken pleasure in representing both as wonderfully low.
p51.zh: 苏格兰许多地方仍然有一群人,称为 " 乡亲 " 或 " 家庭主妇 " ,尽管他们几年前比现在更频繁。 他们是地主和农民的外仆。 他们从主人那里得到的通常的赏金是一栋房子,一个小的园圃,供锅草食用,草木如牛食用,也许还有一亩或两亩的坏耕地. 当他们的主人有机会做工时,他给他们每周两只燕麦,价值约16便士。 在大半年中,他几乎没有机会或根本没有机会从事劳动,种植他们自己的小财产不足以占用他们自己支配的时间。 当这些占领者的人数比现在更多时,据说他们愿意为任何机构微小的补偿而腾出时间,并且为了比其他工人的工资要低。 在古代,它们似乎在欧洲各地都是常见的. 在耕作不良、居住情况更差的国家,大部分地主和农民无法提供本国劳工在某些季节所需的特别多的手。 这些劳工偶尔从主人那里得到的每日或每周的补偿显然不是他们劳动的全部价格。 他们的小房子占了相当大一部分 然而,这种日复一日或周复一日的复议,似乎被许多作家视为整体,他们收集了古代的劳动价格和规定,并且乐于代表两者,都非常低俗.

p52.original: The produce of such labour comes frequently cheaper to market than would otherwise be suitable to its nature. Stockings, in many parts of Scotland, are knit much cheaper than they can anywhere be wrought upon the loom. They are the work of servants and labourers who derive the principal part of their subsistence from some other employment. More than a thousand pair of Shetland stockings are annually imported into Leith, of which the price is from fivepence to seven-pence a pair. At Lerwick, the small capital of the Shetland islands, tenpence a-day, I have been assured, is a common price of common labour. In the same islands, they knit worsted stockings to the value of a guinea a pair and upwards.
p52.zh: 这种劳力的产品往往比其性质更便宜。袜子在苏格兰很多地方的织造价格比在门前任何地方都便宜得多。它们是佣人和劳工的工作,他们的主要生计部分来自其他工作。 每年有一千多双雪特兰丝袜进口到莱思,其中价格从五便士到七便士一对. 在莱威克, 雪特兰群岛的小首都, 每天十便士, 我得到保证, 是一个普通劳动力的共同价格。在同一座岛屿上,它们把最差的袜子织成一对一对豚鼠的值,然后向上。

p53.original: The spinning of linen yarn is carried on in Scotland nearly in the same way as the knitting of stockings, by servants, who are chiefly hired for other purposes. They earn but a very scanty subsistence, who endeavour to get their livelihood by either of those trades. In most parts of Scotland, she is a good spinner who can earn twentypence a-week.
p53.zh: 在苏格兰,亚麻线的旋转几乎与丝袜的织布一样,由主要为其他目的雇用的仆人进行。 他们只挣得很少的生计,他们努力靠其中任何一个行业来谋生。 在苏格兰大部分地区,她是一个很好的旋转者,每周能挣到20便士.

p54.original: In opulent countries, the market is generally so extensive, that any one trade is sufficient to employ the whole labour and stock of those who occupy it. Instances of people living by one employment, and, at the same time, deriving some little advantage from another, occur chiefly in pour countries. The following instance, however, of something of the same kind, is to be found in the capital of a very rich one. There is no city in Europe, I believe, in which house-rent is dearer than in London, and yet I know no capital in which a furnished apartment can be hired so cheap. Lodging is not only much cheaper in London than in Paris; it is much cheaper than in Edinburgh, of the same degree of goodness; and, what may seem extraordinary, the dearness of house-rent is the cause of the cheapness of lodging. The dearness of house-rent in London arises, not only from those causes which render it dear in all great capitals, the dearness of labour, the dearness of all the materials of building, which must generally be brought from a great distance, and, above all, the dearness of ground-rent, every landlord acting the part of a monopolist, and frequently exacting a higher rent for a single acre of bad land in a town, than can be had for a hundred of the best in the country; but it arises in part from the peculiar manners and customs of the people, which oblige every master of a family to hire a whole house from top to bottom. A dwelling-house in England means every thing that is contained under the same roof. In France, Scotland, and many other parts of Europe, it frequently means no more than a single storey. A tradesman in London is obliged to hire a whole house in that part of the town where his customers live. His shop is upon the ground floor, and he and his family sleep in the garret; and he endeavours to pay a part of his house-rent by letting the two middle storeys to lodgers. He expects to maintain his family by his trade, and not by his lodgers. Whereas at Paris and Edinburgh, people who let lodgings have commonly no other means of subsistence; and the price of the lodging must pay, not only the rent of the house, but the whole expense of the family.
p54.zh: 在富裕国家,市场普遍如此广泛,任何一种贸易都足以雇用所有劳动力和拥有者。一个人靠一种工作生活,同时从另一种工作中获得一些微小好处,这种情况主要发生在富裕国家。 然而,在非常富裕的首都,将出现以下类似情况。 我相信,在欧洲没有哪个城市比伦敦更珍贵的房屋租金,然而,我知道没有一个首都可以雇用这么便宜的家具公寓。伦敦的租房价格不仅比巴黎便宜得多;它比爱丁堡的便宜得多,同样程度的好;而且,看来特别的是,住房租金的匮乏是住房价格低廉的原因。伦敦房屋租金的匮乏,不仅产生于那些使它在所有伟大首都都变得珍贵的原因、劳动力的匮乏、建筑材料的匮乏,这些材料一般必须从很远的地方运来,而且最重要的是,地租的匮乏,每个房东都扮演着垄断者的角色,而且常常要为一个城镇一英亩的恶劣土地收取更高的租金,这比全国100个最好的土地要高;而且部分是由于人们的特殊礼仪和习俗,这迫使一个家庭的每个主人从上到下都雇用一整栋房子。英国的住宅是指同一屋檐下的一切东西. 在法国,苏格兰,以及欧洲的许多其他地区,它经常意味着一个单一的商店.伦敦的商人有义务在顾客居住的那部分城市里 雇一整栋房子 他的店铺在一楼,他和家人睡在大衣里;他努力支付一部分房屋租金,让两间中层房屋给住客。 他期望靠他的生意维持家人,而不是靠他的住客维持生计。在巴黎和爱丁堡,租房的人通常没有其他生计手段;而且租房价格不仅必须支付房屋租金,而且必须支付家庭的全部费用。

p55.original: PART II.--Inequalities occasioned by the Policy of Europe.
p55.zh: 第二部分 - 欧洲政策造成的不平等。

p56.original: Such are the inequalities in the whole of the advantages and disadvantages of the different employments of labour and stock, which the defect of any of the three requisites above mentioned must occasion, even where there is the most perfect liberty. But the policy of Europe, by not leaving things at perfect liberty, occasions other inequalities of much greater importance.
p56.zh: 这就是不同劳动和存量就业的利弊整体上的不平等,上述三项条件中的任何一项的缺陷都必须发生,即使有最完美的自由。 但是,欧洲的政策,不把事情置于完全自由的地位,就使其他不平等变得更为重要。

p57.original: It does this chiefly in the three following ways. First, by restraining the competition in some employments to a smaller number than would otherwise be disposed to enter into them; secondly, by increasing it in others beyond what it naturally would be; and, thirdly, by obstructing the free circulation of labour and stock, both from employment to employment, and from place to place.
p57.zh: 它主要以以下三种方式进行这项工作。 首先,将某些职业的竞争限制在数量上,比其他职业要少;其次,将竞争扩大到其他职业,使其超出自然范围;第三,阻碍从就业到就业以及从地方到地方的劳动力和库存的自由流通。

p58.original: First, The policy of Europe occasions a very important inequality in the whole of the advantages and disadvantages of the different employments of labour and stock, by restraining the competition in some employments to a smaller number than might otherwise be disposed to enter into them.
p58.zh: 首先,欧洲的政策将某些职业的竞争限制在数量上,而不是本来可以选择加入这些职业,从而在劳动力和股票的不同就业的利弊方面,造成了一种非常重要的不平等。

p59.original: The exclusive privileges of corporations are the principal means it makes use of for this purpose.
p59.zh: 公司的专属特权是公司为此目的使用的主要手段。

p60.original: The exclusive privilege of an incorporated trade necessarily restrains the competition, in the town where it is established, to those who are free of the trade. To have served an apprenticeship in the town, under a master properly qualified, is commonly the necessary requisite for obtaining this freedom. The bye-laws of the corporation regulate sometimes the number of apprentices which any master is allowed to have, and almost always the number of years which each apprentice is obliged to serve. The intention of both regulations is to restrain the competition to a much smaller number than might otherwise be disposed to enter into the trade. The limitation of the number of apprentices restrains it directly. A long term of apprenticeship restrains it more indirectly, but as effectually, by increasing the expense of education.
p60.zh: 一项合并贸易的专有特权必然限制在设立该贸易的城镇的竞争,而这种竞争只限于那些没有贸易的人。 在镇上从事学徒工作,由具备适当资格的硕士担任学徒,通常是获得这种自由的必要条件。公司的细则有时规定任何主人允许的学徒人数,几乎总是规定每个学徒必须服役的年数。这两项条例的用意是将竞争限制在数量上远小于本来可以选择进入贸易的范围。学徒人数的限制直接限制了学徒人数.长期学徒制更间接地限制了这种教育,但实际上却增加了教育费用。

p61.original: In Sheffield, no master cutler can have more than one apprentice at a time, by a bye-law of the corporation. In Norfolk and Norwich, no master weaver can have more than two apprentices, under pain of forfeiting five pounds a-month to the king. No master hatter can have more than two apprentices anywhere in England, or in the English plantations, under pain of forfeiting; five pounds a-month, half to the king, and half to him who shall sue in any court of record. Both these regulations, though they have been confirmed by a public law of the kingdom, are evidently dictated by the same corporation-spirit which enacted the bye-law of Sheffield. The silk-weavers in London had scarce been incorporated a year, when they enacted a bye-law, restraining any master from having more than two apprentices at a time. It required a particular act of parliament to rescind this bye-law.
p61.zh: 在谢菲尔德,没有一位师傅可以每次拥有一个以上的学徒,通过公司的拜笔法. 在诺福克和诺威奇,没有一个主人编织师能有超过两个学徒,在痛苦中,每个月向国王没收5磅. 在英国任何地方,或在英国种植园,没有一位主帽匠可以拥有超过两个学徒,在丧失财产的痛苦下;每月5磅,一半给国王,一半给在任何记录法庭上起诉的人.这两项条例虽然都得到王国公法的确认,但显然都由同一家公司 -- -- 精神公司所决定,后者颁布了谢菲尔德的细则。伦敦的丝织工很少被并入一年,当时他们颁布了一部拜法,禁止任何主人一次拥有两个以上的学徒. 它要求议会通过一项特别法案来废除这一细则。

p62.original: Seven years seem anciently to have been, all over Europe, the usual term established for the duration of apprenticeships in the greater part of incorporated trades. All such incorporations were anciently called universities, which, indeed, is the proper Latin name for any incorporation whatever. The university of smiths, the university of tailors, etc. are expressions which we commonly meet with in the old charters of ancient towns. When those particular incorporations, which are now peculiarly called universities, were first established, the term of years which it was necessary to study, in order to obtain the degree of master of arts, appears evidently to have been copied from the term of apprenticeship in common trades, of which the incorporations were much more ancient. As to have wrought seven years under a master properly qualified, was necessary, in order to entitle my person to become a master, and to have himself apprentices in a common trade; so to have studied seven years under a master properly qualified, was necessary to entitle him to become a master, teacher, or doctor (words anciently synonymous), in the liberal arts, and to have scholars or apprentices (words likewise originally synonymous) to study under him.
p62.zh: 在欧洲各地,七年似乎古老地成为了在大部分合并行业中学徒期的通常用语。 所有这些公司都是古老的大学,事实上,这些大学是任何公司的正式拉丁名称。铁匠大学,裁缝大学等是我们在古城旧章程中常见的表达方式. 这些特殊公司(现在特别称为大学)最初设立时,为了获得艺术硕士学位,必须学习的年限显然从普通行业的学徒期中复制出来,其中公司更古老。 在一位具有适当资格的大师领导下,已经花了七年时间,这是必要的,这样,我个人才能成为一位大师,并且让自己在普通行业中当学徒;因此,在一位具有适当资格的大师领导下学习了七年,是有必要的,这样他才能成为自由艺术领域的大师、教师或医生(古代同义词),并且有学者或学徒(原始同义词同样是同义词)在他手下学习。

p63.original: By the 5th of Elizabeth, commonly called the Statute of Apprenticeship, it was enacted, that no person should, for the future, exercise any trade, craft, or mystery, at that time exercised in England, unless he had previously served to it an apprenticeship of seven years at least; and what before had been the bye-law of many particular corporations, became in England the general and public law of all trades carried on in market towns. For though the words of the statute are very general, and seem plainly to include the whole kingdom, by interpretation its operation has been limited to market towns; it having been held that, in country villages, a person may exercise several different trades, though he has not served a seven years apprenticeship to each, they being necessary for the conveniency of the inhabitants, and the number of people frequently not being sufficient to supply each with a particular set of hands. By a strict interpretation of the words, too, the operation of this statute has been limited to those trades which were established in England before the 5th of Elizabeth, and has never been extended to such as have been introduced since that time. This limitation has given occasion to several distinctions, which, considered as rules of police, appear as foolish as can well be imagined. It has been adjudged, for example, that a coach-maker can neither himself make nor employ journeymen to make his coach-wheels, but must buy them of a master wheel-wright; this latter trade having been exercised in England before the 5th of Elizabeth. But a wheel-wright, though he has never served an apprenticeship to a coachmaker, may either himself make or employ journeymen to make coaches; the trade of a coachmaker not being within the statute, because not exercised in England at the time when it was made. The manufactures of Manchester, Birmingham, and Wolverhampton, are many of them, upon this account, not within the statute, not having been exercised in England before the 5th of Elizabeth.
p63.zh: 到了伊丽莎白五世(通常称为学徒章程),它颁布,今后任何人都不得在英国从事任何贸易,工艺或神秘活动,除非他以前至少为英格兰服务过七年的学徒;以前许多特定公司的细则在英格兰成为市场城市从事的所有行业的通则和公法. 尽管法规的文字非常笼统,而且似乎显然包括整个王国,但从解释上看,其运作仅限于市场城镇;有人认为,在乡村,一个人可以从事几种不同的行业,虽然他没有为每个行业提供七年的学徒,但这些行业对于居民的宽容是必要的,而且人数往往不足以向每个行业提供特定的手。 通过严格解释这些词语,这个法规的运作也仅限于伊丽莎白五世之前在英国建立的那些行业,并且从未扩展到从那时起引入的那些行业. 这种限制使一些区别成为可能,这些区别被认为是警察的规则,似乎愚蠢得不可想象。 例如,人们判定,教练员本人既不能制造,也不能雇用旅行者制造教练轮,而必须购买主轮机;这种后一种贸易在伊丽莎白五世之前就已经在英国进行. 但是,一个轮子右手虽然从未为教练员提供学徒服务,但可能自己做或雇用旅行员做教练;教练员的交易不在法规范围内,因为当时没有在英格兰行使.曼彻斯特,伯明翰,沃弗汉普顿的制造,都是许多,根据这个理由,不在法规范围内,在伊丽莎白五世之前,在英国没有行使过.

p64.original: In France, the duration of apprenticeships is different in different towns and in different trades. In Paris, five years is the term required in a great number; but, before any person can be qualified to exercise the trade as a master, he must, in many of them, serve five years more as a journeyman. During this latter term, he is called the companion of his master, and the term itself is called his companionship.
p64.zh: 在法国,不同城镇和不同行业的学徒期限不同.在巴黎,5年是很多时候需要的学期;但是,在任何人能够胜任作为主人来锻炼行业之前,他必须在其中的很多时候,再担任5年的旅人. 在后期期间,他被称为主人的同伴,而这个词本身也被称为他的同伴.

p65.original: In Scotland, there is no general law which regulates universally the duration of apprenticeships. The term is different in different corporations. Where it is long, a part of it may generally be redeemed by paying a small fine. In most towns, too, a very small fine is sufficient to purchase the freedom of any corporation. The weavers of linen and hempen cloth, the principal manufactures of the country, as well as all other artificers subservient to them, wheel-makers, reel-makers, etc. may exercise their trades in any town-corporate without paying any fine. In all towns-corporate, all persons are free to sell butchers' meat upon any lawful day of the week. Three years is, in Scotland, a common term of apprenticeship, even in some very nice trades; and, in general, I know of no country in Europe, in which corporation laws are so little oppressive.
p65.zh: 在苏格兰,没有普遍规定学徒期限的一般法律。 在不同的公司中,这个词是不同的。长期存在的地方,一般可以通过缴纳小额罚款赎回一部分. 在大多数城镇,小额罚款也足以购买任何公司的自由。麻布和麻布的织布者,国家的主要制造者,以及服侍他们的其他所有工匠,轮机制造者,皮鞋制造者等,可以在任何镇-公司中锻炼自己的行业,而无需缴纳任何罚款.在所有城镇公司,人人都可以在每周任何合法的日子出售屠夫的肉。 在苏格兰,三年是学徒制的一个常见术语,即使在一些非常不错的行业中也是如此;而且,总的来说,我知道欧洲没有一个国家,在这些国家里,公司法几乎没有什么压迫性。

p66.original: The property which every man has in his own labour, as it is the original foundation of all other property, so it is the most sacred and inviolable. The patrimony of a poor man lies in the strength and dexterity of his hands; and to hinder him from employing this strength and dexterity in what manner he thinks proper, without injury to his neighbour, is a plain violation of this most sacred property. It is a manifest encroachment upon the just liberty, both of the workman, and of those who might be disposed to employ him. As it hinders the one from working at what he thinks proper, so it hinders the others from employing whom they think proper. To judge whether he is fit to be employed, may surely be trusted to the discretion of the employers, whose interest it so much concerns. The affected anxiety of the lawgiver, lest they should employ an improper person, is evidently as impertinent as it is oppressive.
p66.zh: 每个人在自己的劳动中所拥有的财产,因为它是所有其他财产的原始基础,因此是最神圣和不可侵犯的.穷人的遗产在于他的手力和狡猾;并且为了阻止他使用这种力量和狡猾的方式,他认为适当,而不伤害他的邻居,是对这种最神圣财产的公然侵犯. 这显然侵犯了工人和可能愿意雇用他的工人的公正自由。因为它阻碍一个人在他认为合适的地方工作,因此也阻碍其他人雇用他们认为合适的人。 为了判断他是否适合被雇用,可以肯定地相信雇主的酌处权,因为雇主非常关心雇主的利益。受影响的执法人员的焦虑,以免他们雇用不适当的人,显然与压迫性一样无动于衷。

p67.original: The institution of long apprenticeships can give no security that insufficient workmanship shall not frequently be exposed to public sale. When this is done, it is generally the effect of fraud, and not of inability; and the longest apprenticeship can give no security against fraud. Quite different regulations are necessary to prevent this abuse. The sterling mark upon plate, and the stamps upon linen and woollen cloth, give the purchaser much greater security than any statute of apprenticeship. He generally looks at these, but never thinks it worth while to enquire whether the workman had served a seven years apprenticeship.
p67.zh: 长期学徒制不能保证不经常使工作技巧不足而公开出售。这样做时,一般是欺诈的影响,而不是无能力;最长的学徒期不能提供防止欺诈的保障。为防止这种滥用行为,必须制定不同的条例。牌子上的英镑印记和亚麻布和羊毛布上的邮票,使购买者比任何学徒法规都安全得多。 他一般都看这些,但从不认为值得,同时要问一下工人是否已经做了七年的学徒。

p68.original: The institution of long apprenticeships has no tendency to form young people to industry. A journeyman who works by the piece is likely to be industrious, because he derives a benefit from every exertion of his industry. An apprentice is likely to be idle, and almost always is so, because he has no immediate interest to be otherwise. In the inferior employments, the sweets of labour consist altogether in the recompence of labour. They who are soonest in a condition to enjoy the sweets of it, are likely soonest to conceive a relish for it, and to acquire the early habit of industry. A young man naturally conceives an aversion to labour, when for a long time he receives no benefit from it. The boys who are put out apprentices from public charities are generally bound for more than the usual number of years, and they generally turn out very idle and worthless.
p68.zh: 长期学徒制没有形成青年进入工业的倾向. 一个在作品上工作的旅行者 很可能是勤奋的, 因为他从他的行业的每一项努力中都得到了好处。学徒很可能是闲置的,几乎总是闲置的,因为他没有立即的利益去别的地方。 在低级就业中,劳动的甜品完全包括劳动的复工。 他们很快就能享受到它的甜点,他们很可能很快会为它设想一种甜点,并获得工业的早期习惯。年轻人自然会怀有对劳动的厌恶,而长久以来,他得不到任何好处。 从公共慈善机构送出学徒的男孩一般被束缚的时间超过通常的年数,他们通常变得非常闲散和毫无价值。

p69.original: Apprenticeships were altogether unknown to the ancients. The reciprocal duties of master and apprentice make a considerable article in every modern code. The Roman law is perfectly silent with regard to them. I know no Greek or Latin word (I might venture, I believe, to assert that there is none) which expresses the idea we now annex to the word apprentice, a servant bound to work at a particular trade for the benefit of a master, during a term of years, upon condition that the master shall teach him that trade.
p69.zh: 学徒对古人来说是完全未知的.主人公和学徒的相互义务在每一个现代法典中都成为相当重要的条款。罗马法律对他们完全保持沉默。 我并不知道希腊语或拉丁语(我认为,我不敢断言没有),这个词表达了我们现在作为学徒这一词的附件的想法。 学徒是一个在某一行业工作的仆人,必须在某一年的时间内为主人服务,条件是主人要教他这种行业。

p70.original: Long apprenticeships are altogether unnecessary. The arts, which are much superior to common trades, such as those of making clocks and watches, contain no such mystery as to require a long course of instruction. The first invention of such beautiful machines, indeed, and even that of some of the instruments employed in making them, must no doubt have been the work of deep thought and long time, and may justly be considered as among the happiest efforts of human ingenuity. But when both have been fairly invented, and are well understood, to explain to any young man, in the completest manner, how to apply the instruments, and how to construct the machines, cannot well require more than the lessons of a few weeks; perhaps those of a few days might be sufficient. In the common mechanic trades, those of a few days might certainly be sufficient. The dexterity of hand, indeed, even in common trades, cannot be acquired without much practice and experience. But a young man would practice with much more diligence and attention, if from the beginning he wrought as a journeyman, being paid in proportion to the little work which he could execute, and paying in his turn for the materials which he might sometimes spoil through awkwardness and inexperience. His education would generally in this way be more effectual, and always less tedious and expensive. The master, indeed, would be a loser. He would lose all the wages of the apprentice, which he now saves, for seven years together. In the end, perhaps, the apprentice himself would be a loser. In a trade so easily learnt he would have more competitors, and his wages, when he came to be a complete workman, would be much less than at present. The same increase of competition would reduce the profits of the masters, as well as the wages of workmen. The trades, the crafts, the mysteries, would all be losers. But the public would be a gainer, the work of all artificers coming in this way much cheaper to market.
p70.zh: 长期学徒是完全不必要的。艺术比常见的行业,如制钟表,手表等都优越得多,其中并不包含需要长课程的神秘. 这种美丽机器的首次发明,甚至一些制造这些机器所用的仪器的发明,无疑是深思熟虑和长期的工作,可以被公认为人类智慧最幸福的努力之一。 但是,当两者都得到相当的发明,并且被很好地理解,能够以最完整的方式向任何年轻人解释,如何应用仪器,以及如何建造机器,那么,仅仅需要几周的教训是不够的;也许几天的教训就足够了。 在普通的机械行业中,几天的机械行业当然是足够的。 事实上,即使是在普通行业,如果没有大量实践和经验,也无法获得手的狡猾性。 但是,一个年轻人会更加勤奋和关注地练习,如果从一开始他作为一名旅行者,按他能够完成的小工作的比例支付报酬,然后支付他有时可能因尴尬和缺乏经验而破坏的材料。 他的教育一般会这样效果更高,而且总是少些乏味和昂贵.主人的确会是个失败者。 他将失去学徒的全部工资,现在他存了7年的工资。最终,也许,学徒本人会是一个失败者. 在如此容易得知的行业中,他将有更多的竞争者,当他成为一名完全的工人时,他的工资将大大低于现在。竞争的同样增加将减少主人的利润以及工人的工资。行业、工艺、神秘 都会是失败者 但公众会是一个收益者, 所有艺术家的作品 以这种方式走进市场,价格要低得多。

p71.original: It is to prevent his reduction of price, and consequently of wages and profit, by restraining that free competition which would most certainly occasion it, that all corporations, and the greater part of corporation laws have been established. In order to erect a corporation, no other authority in ancient times was requisite, in many parts of Europe, but that of the town-corporate in which it was established. In England, indeed, a charter from the king was likewise necessary. But this prerogative of the crown seems to have been reserved rather for extorting money from the subject, than for the defence of the common liberty against such oppressive monopolies. Upon paying a fine to the king, the charter seems generally to have been readily granted; and when any particular class of artificers or traders thought proper to act as a corporation, without a charter, such adulterine guilds, as they were called, were not always disfranchised upon that account, but obliged to fine annually to the king, for permission to exercise their usurped privileges {See Madox Firma Burgi p. 26 etc.}. The immediate inspection of all corporations, and of the bye-laws which they might think proper to enact for their own government, belonged to the town-corporate in which they were established; and whatever discipline was exercised over them, proceeded commonly, not from the king, but from that greater incorporation of which those subordinate ones were only parts or members.
