p71.zh: 防止他降低价格,从而降低工资和利润,办法是限制自由竞争,这种竞争无疑会引发这种竞争,即所有公司和大部分公司法律都已经确立。 为了建立一家公司,在欧洲许多地方,古代不需要其他权力机构,而需要的是成立公司所在的城镇-公司。 在英国,国王的特许状也是必要的。 但是,王室的这一特权似乎被保留下来,而是为了向主体勒索钱财,而不是为了捍卫共同的自由来对抗这种压迫性的垄断。 在向国王支付罚款后,该特许状似乎一般是很容易得到的;当任何特定阶层的工匠或商人认为作为公司是适当的,没有特许状,他们所说的这种通奸盾并非总被剥离,而是必须每年向国王缴纳罚款,以便允许他们行使被篡夺的特权{见Madox Firma Burgi p.26 等] (英语).立即检查所有公司以及它们可能认为适合为自己的政府颁布的细则,属于它们成立时所在的城镇-公司;无论对公司实行什么纪律,都普遍进行,不是从国王那里,而是从那些附属公司只是其中一部分或成员的更大程度的合并中进行。

p72.original: The government of towns-corporate was altogether in the hands of traders and artificers, and it was the manifest interest of every particular class of them, to prevent the market from being overstocked, as they commonly express it, with their own particular species of industry; which is in reality to keep it always understocked. Each class was eager to establish regulations proper for this purpose, and, provided it was allowed to do so, was willing to consent that every other class should do the same. In consequence of such regulations, indeed, each class was obliged to buy the goods they had occasion for from every other within the town, somewhat dearer than they otherwise might have done. But, in recompence, they were enabled to sell their own just as much dearer; so that, so far it was as broad as long, as they say; and in the dealings of the different classes within the town with one another, none of them were losers by these regulations. But in their dealings with the country they were all great gainers; and in these latter dealings consist the whole trade which supports and enriches every town.
p72.zh: 城镇-公司政府完全掌握在贸易商和工匠的手中,防止市场过度囤积,正如他们通常表达的那样,是他们每一个特定阶层的明确利益所在;事实上,市场总是储存不足。 每个阶层都渴望为此目的制定适当的条例,只要允许,就愿意同意其他各阶层也这样做。 事实上,由于这些条例,每一阶层都有义务从镇内其他各阶层购买他们所购买的货物,这比他们本来可能做的多得多。 但是,作为补偿,他们能够像他们那样卖掉自己的东西;这样,就如同他们所说的那样,它的范围很广;在城镇内部不同阶层之间的交往中,没有一个是这些条例的输家。 但是,在他们与这个国家的交往中,他们都是大赢家;在后一种交易中,他们包括支持和丰富每个城镇的整个贸易。

p73.original: Every town draws its whole subsistence, and all the materials of its industry, from the: country. It pays for these chiefly in two ways. First, by sending back to the country a part of those materials wrought up and manufactured; in which case, their price is augmented by the wages of the workmen, and the profits of their masters or immediate employers; secondly, by sending to it a part both of the rude and manufactured produce, either of other countries, or of distant parts of the same country, imported into the town; in which case, too, the original price of those goods is augmented by the wages of the carriers or sailors, and by the profits of the merchants who employ them. In what is gained upon the first of those branches of commerce, consists the advantage which the town makes by its manufactures; in what is gained upon the second, the advantage of its inland and foreign trade. The wages of the workmen, and the profits of their different employers, make up the whole of what is gained upon both. Whatever regulations, therefore, tend to increase those wages and profits beyond what they otherwise: would be, tend to enable the town to purchase, with a smaller quantity of its labour, the produce of a greater quantity of the labour of the country. They give the traders and artificers in the town an advantage over the landlords, farmers, and labourers, in the country, and break down that natural equality which would otherwise take place in the commerce which is carried on between them. The whole annual produce of the labour of the society is annually divided between those two different sets of people. By means of those regulations, a greater share of it is given to the inhabitants of the town than would otherwise fall to them, and a less to those of' the country.
p73.zh: 每个城镇都从以下国家获得其全部生计及其工业的所有材料: 它主要通过两种方式支付这些费用。 首先,将制造和制造的部分材料运回本国;在这种情况下,其价格由工人的工资及其主人或直系雇主的利润增加;其次,将进口到镇上的粗鲁和制成品的一部分,即其他国家或同一个国家的遥远地区的一部分运回本国;在这种情况下,这些货物的原价也由承运人或水手的工资以及雇用这些产品的商人的利润增加。 在第一个商业分支所获得的利益中,包括该镇的制成品带来的优势;在第二个分支所获得的利益中,包括内陆和外贸的优势。工人的工资及其不同雇主的利润,构成双方所得的全部收益。 因此,无论实行何种条例,都往往使这些工资和利润增加,超出原来的水平:如果城镇劳动力数量较少,就能够购买该国更多劳动力的农产品。 它们使镇上的商人和工匠比国内的地主、农民和劳工更有利,并打破了本来在他们之间进行的商业活动中存在的自然平等。社会劳动力的整个年度产量每年在这两组人之间分配。 根据这些条例,城镇居民得到的津贴比他们得不到的要多,而国家居民得到的津贴则更少。

p74.original: The price which the town really pays for the provisions and materials annually imported into it, is the quantity of manufactures and other goods annually exported from it. The dearer the latter are sold, the cheaper the former are bought. The industry of the town becomes more, and that of the country less advantageous.
p74.zh: 城镇每年进口的物品和材料的实际价格是每年从城镇出口的制成品和其他货物的数量。后者的销量越少,前者的销价就越低廉.镇上的工业越来越发达,而国家的工业则不那么有利。

p75.original: That the industry which is carried on in towns is, everywhere in Europe, more advantageous than that which is carried on in the country, without entering into any very nice computations, we may satisfy ourselves by one very simple and obvious observation. In every country of Europe, we find at least a hundred people who have acquired great fortunes, from small beginnings, by trade and manufactures, the industry which properly belongs to towns, for one who has done so by that which properly belongs to the country, the raising of rude produce by the improvement and cultivation of land. Industry, therefore, must be better rewarded, the wages of labour and the profits of stock must evidently be greater, in the one situation than in the other. But stock and labour naturally seek the most advantageous employment. They naturally, therefore, resort as much as they can to the town, and desert the country.
p75.zh: 在城镇中进行的工业,在欧洲各地,比在国内进行的工业更有利, 不进行任何非常好的计算, 我们也许可以用一个非常简单和明显的观察来满足自己。在欧洲每一个国家,我们发现至少有一百人从小开始,通过贸易和制造,从属于城镇的工业,获得了巨大的财富,对于通过属于国家的工业,通过改良和耕种土地来饲养粗鲁的农产品,已经这样做了. 因此,工业必须获得更好的奖励,劳动力工资和股票利润显然必须比另一种情况要高。 但是,股票和劳动力自然寻求最有利的就业。 因此,他们自然会尽可能多地到镇上,并逃离国家。

p76.original: The inhabitants of a town being collected into one place, can easily combine together. The most insignificant trades carried on in towns have, accordingly, in some place or other, been incorporated; and even where they have never been incorporated, yet the corporation-spirit, the jealousy of strangers, the aversion to take apprentices, or to communicate the secret of their trade, generally prevail in them, and often teach them, by voluntary associations and agreements, to prevent that free competition which they cannot prohibit by bye-laws. The trades which employ but a small number of hands, run most easily into such combinations. Half-a-dozen wool-combers, perhaps, are necessary to keep a thousand spinners and weavers at work. By combining not to take apprentices, they can not only engross the employment, but reduce the whole manufacture into a sort of slavery to themselves, and raise the price of their labour much above what is due to the nature of their work.
p76.zh: 被收集到一个城镇的居民可以很容易地结合在一起. 因此,城镇中从事的最微不足道的行业,在某些地方或其他地方,已经注册;即使从未注册,但公司精神、陌生人的嫉妒、不愿收徒弟或不愿传播其行业的秘密,在城镇中普遍占上风,而且往往通过自愿协会和协议来教育他们,防止他们无法禁止的附则自由竞争。使用少量手的行业最容易形成这种组合。半个十几只羊毛圈 可能是保持一千个旋转器和编织器工作所必需的 通过不收学徒,他们不仅可以把就业集中起来,而且可以把整个制造过程变成一种自我奴役,并且把劳动价格提高到远远高于工作性质所决定的。

p77.original: The inhabitants of the country, dispersed in distant places, cannot easily combine together. They have not only never been incorporated, but the incorporation spirit never has prevailed among them. No apprenticeship has ever been thought necessary to qualify for husbandry, the great trade of the country. After what are called the fine arts, and the liberal professions, however, there is perhaps no trade which requires so great a variety of knowledge and experience. The innumerable volumes which have been written upon it in all languages, may satisfy us, that among the wisest and most learned nations, it has never been regarded as a matter very easily understood. And from all those volumes we shall in vain attempt to collect that knowledge of its various and complicated operations which is commonly possessed even by the common farmer; how contemptuously soever the very contemptible authors of some of them may sometimes affect to speak of him. There is scarce any common mechanic trade, on the contrary, of which all the operations may not be as completely and distinctly explained in a pamphlet of a very few pages, as it is possible for words illustrated by figures to explain them. In the history of the arts, now publishing by the French Academy of Sciences, several of them are actually explained in this manner. The direction of operations, besides, which must be varied with every change of the weather, as well as with many other accidents, requires much more judgment and discretion, than that of those which are always the same, or very nearly the same.
p77.zh: 该国居民分散在遥远的地方,他们无法轻易地结合在一起。 它们不仅从未被纳入其中,而且从来也没有融入精神。据认为,没有任何学徒资格成为国家大行业的畜牧业。 然而,在所谓的美术和自由职业之后,也许没有贸易需要如此丰富的知识和经验。以各种语言写成的无数卷本可能令我们感到满意的是,在最明智和最博学的国家中,它从未被视为一个非常容易理解的问题。 我们将从所有这些书中徒劳地收集甚至普通农民通常拥有的各种复杂操作的知识;其中一些非常可鄙的作者有时会如何轻蔑地影响谈论他。 相反,几乎没有任何普通的机械工贸易,而所有业务都可能无法在几页的小册子中完整和明确地加以解释,因为用数字来说明的文字是能够解释的。 在艺术史上,现由法国科学院出版,其中几部实际上都是以这种方式解释的. 此外,随着天气的改变以及许多其他事故的发生,行动的方向必须有所不同,这需要比那些总是一样或几乎一样的判断力和裁量力要大得多。

p78.original: Not only the art of the farmer, the general direction of the operations of husbandry, but many inferior branches of country labour require much more skill and experience than the greater part of mechanic trades. The man who works upon brass and iron, works with instruments, and upon materials of which the temper is always the same, or very nearly the same. But the man who ploughs the ground with a team of horses or oxen, works with instruments of which the health, strength, and temper, are very different upon different occasions. The condition of the materials which he works upon, too, is as variable as that of the instruments which he works with, and both require to be managed with much judgment and discretion. The common ploughman, though generally regarded as the pattern of stupidity and ignorance, is seldom defective in this judgment and discretion. He is less accustomed, indeed, to social intercourse, than the mechanic who lives in a town. His voice and language are more uncouth, and more difficult to be understood by those who are not used to them. His understanding, however, being accustomed to consider a greater variety of objects, is generally much superior to that of the other, whose whole attention, from morning till night, is commonly occupied in performing one or two very simple operations. How much the lower ranks of people in the country are really superior to those of the town, is well known to every man whom either business or curiosity has led to converse much with both. In China and Indostan, accordingly, both the rank and the wages of country labourers are said to be superior to those of the greater part of artificers and manufacturers. They would probably be so everywhere, if corporation laws and the corporation spirit did not prevent it.
p78.zh: 不仅农民的艺术,畜牧业经营的总方向,而且国内许多劣等的劳动部门都需要比大部分机械行业更多的技能和经验. 在铜和铁上工作的人 用乐器工作, 和材料, 脾气总是一样,或者几乎一样。 但是,用一队马或牛犁地的人,用各种工具工作,其中健康,体力,脾气,在不同场合都有很大不同. 他所研究的材料的条件也与他所研究的仪器一样多变,两者都需要以很大的判断力和酌处权加以管理。普通的犁人虽然一般被认为是愚蠢和无知的规律,但在这种判断和裁量中很少有缺陷. 实际上,他比住在一个城镇的机械师更不习惯社交。 他的语音和语言更加不协调,更难以被那些不习惯的人理解. 然而,他的理解习惯于考虑更多种类的物体,一般比另一个要优越得多,后者从早上到晚上,在进行一两次非常简单的行动时,通常都全神贯注. 全国的低层人物比镇上的人要高得多, 因此,在中国和印度斯坦,据说乡村劳工的级别和工资都优于大部分艺术家和制造商的级别和工资。 如果公司法和公司精神不阻止,它们可能随处可见。

p79.original: The superiority which the industry of the towns has everywhere in Europe over that of the country, is not altogether owing to corporations and corporation laws. It is supported by many other regulations. The high duties upon foreign manufactures, and upon all goods imported by alien merchants, all tend to the same purpose. Corporation laws enable the inhabitants of towns to raise their prices, without fearing to be undersold by the free competition of their own countrymen. Those other regulations secure them equally against that of foreigners. The enhancement of price occasioned by both is everywhere finally paid by the landlords, farmers, and labourers, of the country, who have seldom opposed the establishment of such monopolies. They have commonly neither inclination nor fitness to enter into combinations; and the clamour and sophistry of merchants and manufacturers easily persuade them, that the private interest of a part, and of a subordinate part, of the society, is the general interest of the whole.
p79.zh: 在欧洲各地,城镇工业的优越性并不完全由于公司和公司的法律。 它得到了许多其他条例的支持。 对外国制成品和外国商人进口的所有货物征收高额关税,目的都相同。公司法使城镇居民能够提高物价,而不必担心自己乡民的自由竞争会让其低价出售. 其他条例保障他们与外国人平等。两国价格的提高最终都由该国地主、农民和劳工支付,他们很少反对建立这种垄断。 他们通常既不愿意也不适宜组合;商人和制造商的喧闹和索菲斯主义很容易说服他们,认为社会的一部分和附属部分的私人利益是整个社会的普遍利益。

p80.original: In Great Britain, the superiority of the industry of the towns over that of the country seems to have been greater formerly than in the present times. The wages of country labour approach nearer to those of manufacturing labour, and the profits of stock employed in agriculture to those of trading and manufacturing stock, than they are said to have none in the last century, or in the beginning of the present. This change may be regarded as the necessary, though very late consequence of the extraordinary encouragement given to the industry of the towns. The stocks accumulated in them come in time to be so great, that it can no longer be employed with the ancient profit in that species of industry which is peculiar to them. That industry has its limits like every other; and the increase of stock, by increasing the competition, necessarily reduces the profit. The lowering of profit in the town forces out stock to the country, where, by creating a new demand for country labour, it necessarily raises its wages. It then spreads itself, if I my say so, over the face of the land, and, by being employed in agriculture, is in part restored to the country, at the expense of which, in a great measure, it had originally been accumulated in the town. That everywhere in Europe the greatest improvements of the country have been owing to such over flowings of the stock originally accumulated in the towns, I shall endeavour to shew hereafter, and at the same time to demonstrate, that though some countries have, by this course, attained to a considerable degree of opulence, it is in itself necessarily slow, uncertain, liable to be disturbed and interrupted by innumerable accidents, and, in every respect, contrary to the order of nature and of reason. The interests, prejudices, laws, and customs, which have given occasion to it, I shall endeavour to explain as fully and distinctly as I can in the third and fourth books of this Inquiry.
p80.zh: 在大不列颠,城镇工业比国家工业的优越性似乎比现在更为突出.国家劳动力的工资接近制造业劳动力的工资,农业所雇股票的利润接近贸易和制造业的利润,据说在上个世纪或现在的初期,这些利润是没有的。 这一变化可能被视为必要的,尽管由于对城镇工业的特别鼓励而导致的很晚的结果。积存的股票是及时的 如此之大, 以至于它不能再用 古老的利润 在这种行业 中,这是他们特有的。 这个行业有其极限,就像其他行业一样;股票的增加,通过增加竞争,必然会减少利润。城镇利润的下降迫使该国向国外倾斜,通过创造对国家劳动力的新需求,该国必然提高工资。然则其流散,若我所言,则遍及土地之面,而因务农之业,则部分复于国,而其费之,大可谓原积于镇矣. 欧洲各地最大的改善是由于原先在城镇积累的股票流出过多,因此,我将在以后努力展示,同时要表明,虽然一些国家通过这一途径已经相当富足,但其本身必然是缓慢、不确定的,可能会受到无数事故的干扰和干扰,而且无论在什么方面,都与自然和理智的先后次序背道而驰。 我将努力在本调查的第三和第四本书中尽可能全面和明确地解释给予它机会的利益、偏见、法律和习俗。

p81.original: People of the same trade seldom meet together, even for merriment and diversion, but the conversation ends in a conspiracy against the public, or in some contrivance to raise prices. It is impossible, indeed, to prevent such meetings, by any law which either could be executed, or would be consistent with liberty and justice. But though the law cannot hinder people of the same trade from sometimes assembling together, it ought to do nothing to facilitate such assemblies, much less to render them necessary.
p81.zh: 同一行业的人很少聚在一起,即使是为了取悦和转移注意力,但谈话最后还是以阴谋反对公众或某种阴谋来提高价格。 实际上,任何法律都不可能阻止这种会面,因为任何法律要么可以执行,要么符合自由和正义。 但是,虽然法律不能阻止同一行业的人有时聚集在一起,但法律不应为这种集会提供便利,更不能使这种集会成为必要。

p82.original: A regulation which obliges all those of the same trade in a particular town to enter their names and places of abode in a public register, facilitates such assemblies. It connects individuals who might never otherwise be known to one another, and gives every man of the trade a direction where to find every other man of it.
p82.zh: 一项规定规定,在特定城镇的同一行业的所有人必须在公共登记册上登记其姓名和居住地,为这种集会提供便利。 它将可能永远无法互相认识的个人联系起来,并给每个贸易者一个找到其他贸易者的方向。

p83.original: A regulation which enables those of the same trade to tax themselves, in order to provide for their poor, their sick, their widows and orphans, by giving them a common interest to manage, renders such assemblies necessary.
p83.zh: 一项使同一行业的人能够自我征税的条例使得这种集会成为必要,以便通过给予他们共同的管理利益来照顾他们的穷人、病人、寡妇和孤儿。

p84.original: An incorporation not only renders them necessary, but makes the act of the majority binding upon the whole. In a free trade, an effectual combination cannot be established but by the unanimous consent of every single trader, and it cannot last longer than every single trader continues of the same mind. The majority of a corporation can enact a bye-law, with proper penalties, which will limit the competition more effectually and more durably than any voluntary combination whatever.
p84.zh: 合并不仅使这些要素成为必要,而且使多数人的行为对整体具有约束力。 在自由贸易中,有效的组合是不能确定的,但必须得到每个贸易商的一致同意,而且其持续时间不能超过每个贸易商继续持同一想法。多数公司可以颁布附带法,规定适当的惩罚,这将比任何自愿结合的做法更有效、更持久地限制竞争。

p85.original: The pretence that corporations are necessary for the better government of the trade, is without any foundation. The real and effectual discipline which is exercised over a workman, is not that of his corporation, but that of his customers. It is the fear of losing their employment which restrains his frauds and corrects his negligence. An exclusive corporation necessarily weakens the force of this discipline. A particular set of workmen must then be employed, let them behave well or ill. It is upon this account that, in many large incorporated towns, no tolerable workmen are to be found, even in some of the most necessary trades. If you would have your work tolerably executed, it must be done in the suburbs, where the workmen, having no exclusive privilege, have nothing but their character to depend upon, and you must then smuggle it into the town as well as you can.
p85.zh: 公司是更好地管理贸易所必需的借口,这是没有根据的。 对工人实行的真正有效的纪律不是他的公司,而是他的客户。 正是害怕失去工作,才限制了他的欺诈行为,纠正了他的疏忽。独家公司必然削弱这一纪律的力量。 然后必须雇用特定的工人,让他们表现良好或生病。 正是由于这个原因,在许多大型城镇,即使在一些最必要的行业中,也找不到可以容忍的工人。 如果你能容忍地完成你的工作,它必须在郊区完成,在那里,工人没有专属特权,除了他们的品格外,别无他法,然后你必须尽你所能把它偷运到镇上。

p86.original: It is in this manner that the policy of Europe, by restraining the competition in some employments to a smaller number than would otherwise be disposed to enter into them, occasions a very important inequality in the whole of the advantages and disadvantages of the different employments of labour and stock.
p86.zh: 正是以这种方式,欧洲的政策将某些职业的竞争限制在数量上,而不是本来打算加入的,从而在劳动力和股票的不同职业的利弊方面,出现了一种非常重要的不平等。

p87.original: Secondly, The policy of Europe, by increasing the competition in some employments beyond what it naturally would be, occasions another inequality, of an opposite kind, in the whole of the advantages and disadvantages of the different employments of labour and stock.
p87.zh: 其次,欧洲的政策是,在某些职业中,竞争的增加超出了自然可能发生的另一种不平等,而这种不平等则与不同的劳动和股票就业的利弊大相径庭。

p88.original: It has been considered as of so much importance that a proper number of young people should be educated for certain professions, that sometimes the public, and sometimes the piety of private founders, have established many pensions, scholarships, exhibitions, bursaries, etc. for this purpose, which draw many more people into those trades than could otherwise pretend to follow them. In all Christian countries, I believe, the education of the greater part of churchmen is paid for in this manner. Very few of them are educated altogether at their own expense. The long, tedious, and expensive education, therefore, of those who are, will not always procure them a suitable reward, the church being crowded with people, who, in order to get employment, are willing to accept of a much smaller recompence than what such an education would otherwise have entitled them to; and in this manner the competition of the poor takes away the reward of the rich. It would be indecent, no doubt, to compare either a curate or a chaplain with a journeyman in any common trade. The pay of a curate or chaplain, however, may very properly be considered as of the same nature with the wages of a journeyman. They are all three paid for their work according to the contract which they may happen to make with their respective superiors. Till after the middle of the fourteenth century, five merks, containing about as much silver as ten pounds of our present money, was in England the usual pay of a curate or a stipendiary parish priest, as we find it regulated by the decrees of several different national councils. At the same period, fourpence a-day, containing the same quantity of silver as a shilling of our present money, was declared to be the pay of a master mason; and threepence a-day, equal to ninepence of our present money, that of a journeyman mason. {See the Statute of Labourers, 25, Ed. III.} The wages of both these labourer's, therefore, supposing them to have been constantly employed, were much superior to those of the curate. The wages of the master mason, supposing him to have been without employment one-third of the year, would have fully equalled them. By the 12th of Queen Anne, c. 12. it is declared, "That whereas, for want of sufficient maintenance and encouragement to curates, the cures have, in several places, been meanly supplied, the bishop is, therefore, empowered to appoint, by writing under his hand and seal, a sufficient certain stipend or allowance, not exceeding fifty, and not less than twenty pounds a-year". Forty pounds a-year is reckoned at present very good pay for a curate; and, notwithstanding this act of parliament, there are many curacies under twenty pounds a-year. There are journeymen shoemakers in London who earn forty pounds a-year, and there is scarce an industrious workman of any kind in that metropolis who does not earn more than twenty. This last sum, indeed, does not exceed what frequently earned by common labourers in many country parishes. Whenever the law has attempted to regulate the wages of workmen, it has always been rather to lower them than to raise them. But the law has, upon many occasions, attempted to raise the wages of curates, and, for the dignity of the church, to oblige the rectors of parishes to give them more than the wretched maintenance which they themselves might be willing to accept of. And, in both cases, the law seems to have been equally ineffectual, and has never either been able to raise the wages of curates, or to sink those of labourers to the degree that was intended; because it has never been able to hinder either the one from being willing to accept of less than the legal allowance, on account of the indigence of their situation and the multitude of their competitors, or the other from receiving more, on account of the contrary competition of those who expected to derive either profit or pleasure from employing them.
p88.zh: 据认为,相当数量的年轻人应当接受某些职业的教育,有时是公众,有时是私人创办人的虔诚,为此建立了许多养老金、奖学金、展览、奖学金等,这吸引了更多的人从事这些行业,而不是假想跟踪他们。 我相信,在所有基督教国家,对大部分教会人士的教育都是以这种方式支付的。 她们当中很少有人完全自费接受教育。 因此,那些长期、乏味和昂贵的教育不会总是给他们带来适当的奖励,教堂里挤满了人,为了获得就业,他们愿意接受比这种教育本来应该给他们的回报要小得多的补偿;这样,穷人的竞争就夺走了富人的奖励。 毫无疑问,在任何普通行业中,将馆长或牧师与旅行人员进行比较都是不体面的。 然而,可以非常恰当地将一名院长或牧师的薪酬视为与一名旅行者的工资具有同等性质。这三个人都是根据他们与各自上级订立的合同而领取工资的。 直到14世纪中叶, 5个默克, 包含大约10磅的银子, 我们目前的钱, 在英格兰是通常的 领主或领薪教区牧师的薪水,同一时期,每天四便士的银币数量与我们现钱的先令相同,被宣布为泥匠大师的薪水;每天三便士,相当于我们现钱的九便士,相当于旅行者泥匠的薪水。 {参见劳工章程,25, Ed. 因此,这两个工人的工资,假定他们一直受雇于工会,比总管的工资高得多。工匠主的工资,假定他一年中三分之一没有工作,本来是完全相等的.至安皇后十二世时,c.12. 宣布:"虽然由于缺乏足够的维持和鼓励来治病,在几个地方的治疗方法都得到了廉价的供给,但主教因此被授权通过手和封印书写,指定足够的一定的津贴或津贴,每年不超过50,不少于20磅". 目前,每年40磅被计算为一个院士的薪酬非常高;尽管议会采取了这一行动,但每年仍有许多院士不到20磅。伦敦有一些旅行者鞋匠每年挣40磅, 而在这个大都会里,几乎没有一个勤奋的工人, 他们的收入不超过20美元。 实际上,最后一笔金额不超过许多国家教区普通劳工经常挣得的数额。每当法律试图规范工人的工资时,总是倾向于降低工资,而不是提高工资。 但是,法律在许多场合都试图提高教士的工资,为了教会的尊严,要求教区长给予他们比他们自己可能愿意接受的可悲的赡养费更多的钱。 而且,在这两种情况下,法律似乎都同样无效,而且从来没有能够提高科长的工资,或者使劳工的工资降到原定的水平;因为法律从来没有能够阻止他们愿意接受低于法律津贴,因为他们的贫困处境和竞争对手众多,或者由于希望从雇用他们中获得利润或乐趣的人的相反竞争而阻止他们接受更多的津贴。

p89.original: The great benefices and other ecclesiastical dignities support the honour of the church, notwithstanding the mean circumstances of some of its inferior members. The respect paid to the profession, too, makes some compensation even to them for the meanness of their pecuniary recompence. In England, and in all Roman catholic countries, the lottery of the church is in reality much more advantageous than is necessary. The example of the churches of Scotland, of Geneva, and of several other protestant churches, may satisfy us, that in so creditable a profession, in which education is so easily procured, the hopes of much more moderate benefices will draw a sufficient number of learned, decent, and respectable men into holy orders.
p89.zh: 伟大的教友和其他教会的尊贵支持教会的荣誉,尽管其一些低等成员的情况十分恶劣.给予该职业的尊敬,甚至使他们得到一些补偿,因为他们的金钱补偿是卑鄙的。 在英国,以及所有罗马天主教国家,教会的彩票实际上比必要的要有利得多.苏格兰教会、日内瓦教会和其他一些抗议教会的例子可能使我们感到满意,在如此值得称道的行业中,教育如此容易获得,而更温和的仁爱的希望将吸引足够多的有学识、体面和可敬的人加入神圣的秩序。

p90.original: In professions in which there are no benefices, such as law and physic, if an equal proportion of people were educated at the public expense, the competition would soon be so great as to sink very much their pecuniary reward. It might then not be worth any man's while to educate his son to either of those professions at his own expense. They would be entirely abandoned to such as had been educated by those public charities, whose numbers and necessities would oblige them in general to content themselves with a very miserable recompence, to the entire degradation of the now respectable professions of law and physic.
p90.zh: 在没有恩惠的职业中,如法律和体操,如果有同等比例的人以公费接受教育,那么竞争很快会非常激烈,以致于他们的金钱报酬大打折扣。那样的话,教育他的儿子学习任何一种职业,都是不值得的,他要自己花钱。 这些公共慈善机构所教育的慈善机构将完全放弃它们,这些机构的数量和需要将迫使它们普遍满足于非常悲惨的复职,满足于现在受人尊敬的法律和体格职业的完全退化。

p91.original: That unprosperous race of men, commonly called men of letters, are pretty much in the situation which lawyers and physicians probably would be in, upon the foregoing supposition. In every part of Europe, the greater part of them have been educated for the church, but have been hindered by different reasons from entering into holy orders. They have generally, therefore, been educated at the public expense; and their numbers are everywhere so great, as commonly to reduce the price of their labour to a very paltry recompence.
p91.zh: 这种不愉快的男子种族,通常称为信差,几乎处于律师和医生可能所处的境地,根据上述假设。在欧洲的每一个地区,他们中的大部分人都接受了教会的教育,但因不同的原因阻碍了他们进入圣令. 因此,他们一般都以公费接受教育;他们的人数在任何地方都如此之多,通常是为了把劳动力的价格降低到微不足道的复工水平。

p92.original: Before the invention of the art of printing, the only employment by which a man of letters could make any thing by his talents, was that of a public or private teacher, or by communicating to other people the curious and useful knowledge which he had acquired himself; and this is still surely a more honourable, a more useful, and, in general, even a more profitable employment than that other of writing for a bookseller, to which the art of printing has given occasion. The time and study, the genius, knowledge, and application requisite to qualify an eminent teacher of the sciences, are at least equal to what is necessary for the greatest practitioners in law and physic. But the usual reward of the eminent teacher bears no proportion to that of the lawyer or physician, because the trade of the one is crowded with indigent people, who have been brought up to it at the public expense; whereas those of the other two are encumbered with very few who have not been educated at their own. The usual recompence, however, of public and private teachers, small as it may appear, would undoubtedly be less than it is, if the competition of those yet more indigent men of letters, who write for bread, was not taken out of the market. Before the invention of the art of printing, a scholar and a beggar seem to have been terms very nearly synonymous. The different governors of the universities, before that time, appear to have often granted licences to their scholars to beg.
p92.zh: 在发明印刷艺术之前,只有公用或私人的教师才能用书信的人才能做任何事情;或者通过向其他人传达他自己获得的好奇和有用的知识;这无疑仍然是更光荣,更有用,而且总的来说,比起为书商写作的另一种更有利可图的工作,印刷艺术给了这种机会.时间和学习、才智、知识和应用是取得著名科学教师资格的必要条件,至少等于最伟大的法律和物理实践者所需要的时间和学习。 但是,杰出教师的通常报酬与律师或医生的奖励不相称,因为前者的行业挤满了穷人,这些人是靠公费抚养的;而另外两人的行业则只有极少数人没有受过自己的教育。 但是,如果那些为面包书写的更贫穷的书信教师的竞争没有被赶出市场,那么,公共和私人教师通常的复职率,尽管看起来可能很小,但无疑会比现在要低。 在印刷艺术发明之前,一位学者和乞丐似乎几乎是同义词.在此之前,各大学的不同校长似乎经常向其学者发放乞讨许可证.

p93.original: In ancient times, before any charities of this kind had been established for the education of indigent people to the learned professions, the rewards of eminent teachers appear to have been much more considerable. Isocrates, in what is called his discourse against the sophists, reproaches the teachers of his own times with inconsistency. "They make the most magnificent promises to their scholars," says he, "and undertake to teach them to be wise, to be happy, and to be just; and, in return for so important a service, they stipulate the paltry reward of four or five minae." "They who teach wisdom," continues he, "ought certainly to be wise themselves; but if any man were to sell such a bargain for such a price, he would be convicted of the most evident folly." He certainly does not mean here to exaggerate the reward, and we may be assured that it was not less than he represents it. Four minae were equal to thirteen pounds six shillings and eightpence; five minae to sixteen pounds thirteen shillings and fourpence. Something not less than the largest of those two sums, therefore, must at that time have been usually paid to the most eminent teachers at Athens. Isocrates himself demanded ten minae, or £ 33:6:8 from each scholar. When he taught at Athens, he is said to have had a hundred scholars. I understand this to be the number whom he taught at one time, or who attended what we would call one course of lectures; a number which will not appear extraordinary from so great a city to so famous a teacher, who taught, too, what was at that time the most fashionable of all sciences, rhetoric. He must have made, therefore, by each course of lectures, a thousand minae, or £ 3335:6:8. A thousand minae, accordingly, is said by Plutarch, in another place, to have been his didactron, or usual price of teaching. Many other eminent teachers in those times appear to have acquired great fortunes. Georgias made a present to the temple of Delphi of his own statue in solid gold. We must not, I presume, suppose that it was as large as the life. His way of living, as well as that of Hippias and Protagoras, two other eminent teachers of those times, is represented by Plato as splendid, even to ostentation. Plato himself is said to have lived with a good deal of magnificence. Aristotle, after having been tutor to Alexander, and most munificently rewarded, as it is universally agreed, both by him and his father, Philip, thought it worth while, notwithstanding, to return to Athens, in order to resume the teaching of his school. Teachers of the sciences were probably in those times less common than they came to be in an age or two afterwards, when the competition had probably somewhat reduced both the price of their labour and the admiration for their persons. The most eminent of them, however, appear always to have enjoyed a degree of consideration much superior to any of the like profession in the present times. The Athenians sent Carneades the academic, and Diogenes the stoic, upon a solemn embassy to Rome; and though their city had then declined from its former grandeur, it was still an independent and considerable republic.
p93.zh: 在古代,在建立这类慈善机构将穷人教育到有学识的职业之前,杰出教师的奖励似乎要大得多。异教徒在所谓的他反对 sophists 的言论中, 指责自己时代的老师 不一致。"他们对他们的学者做了最伟大的承诺",他说:"他们承诺教他们聪明,快乐,公正;作为回报,他们规定四五灵敏的微薄报酬。"他继续说:"他们教他们智慧,他们自己必定是聪明的;如果有人为这种代价出卖这种交易,他必定被判定为最明显的愚昧的人。"他当然无意在这里夸大报酬,我们也许可以保证,报酬不会少于他所代表的报酬。4米内等于13磅6先令和8便士;5米内等于16磅13先令和4便士. 因此,在那时,通常必须向雅典最杰出的教师支付不少于这两笔款项中最大的一笔。 伊索格拉特本人要求10米内,即每个学者给予33:6:8英镑. 在雅典教书时,据说他有一百名学者. 我理解这是他曾经教过的人,或者参加过我们称之为一门课程的讲课的人;从如此伟大的城市到如此著名的教师,这个数字看起来并不特别,他也教过当时最时髦的科学和修辞。 因此,他肯定通过每次讲座,都做了一千米纳,即3335:6:8. 因此,普鲁塔克在另一个地方说,一千米是他的教费,或通常的教费。 当时的许多其他著名教师似乎都获得了巨大的财富。乔治亚人用坚固的金币为自己雕像的德尔斐神庙做了礼物. 我想,我们决不能认为它和生命一样大。 他的生活方式,以及那些时代的另外两位杰出教师希皮亚斯和普罗塔戈拉斯的生活方式,都以柏拉图为代表,甚至表现得非常出色。柏拉图本人据说生活过着丰厚的壮观.亚里士多德在担任亚历山大的导师后,而且得到的奖励也最多,他和父亲菲利普都普遍同意,尽管如此,他还是认为返回雅典是值得的,以便恢复他学校的教学.理科教师在那些时期可能比在之后的一两岁时更不常见,当时的竞争可能降低了他们的劳动价格和对其个人的钦佩。 然而,其中最杰出者似乎在当今时代一直享有比任何类似职业高得多的考虑。雅典人将学术家卡内亚德斯和斯图克人狄欧根尼斯送到罗马的庄严大使馆;虽然他们的城市后来从以前的盛大时期就已经衰落了,但它仍然是一个独立和相当的共和国.

p94.original: Carneades, too, was a Babylonian by birth; and as there never was a people more jealous of admitting foreigners to public offices than the Athenians, their consideration for him must have been very great.
p94.zh: 卡内亚德斯也是出身的巴比伦人;由于从未有过比雅典人更嫉妒接纳外国人担任公职的民族,所以他们对他的考虑一定非常大.

p95.original: This inequality is, upon the whole, perhaps rather advantageous than hurtful to the public. It may somewhat degrade the profession of a public teacher; but the cheapness of literary education is surely an advantage which greatly overbalances this trifling inconveniency. The public, too, might derive still greater benefit from it, if the constitution of those schools and colleges, in which education is carried on, was more reasonable than it is at present through the greater part of Europe.
p95.zh: 总的来说,这种不平等也许对公众有利而不是有害。 这可能会在一定程度上贬低公共教师的职业;但文学教育的廉价性无疑是一个优势,它大大地过度平衡了这种三重不便的现象。 如果教育所在的学校和学院的章程比目前欧洲大部分地区的宪法更加合理,公众也可能从中获益更大。

p96.original: Thirdly, the policy of Europe, by obstructing the free circulation of labour and stock, both from employment to employment, and from place to place, occasions, in some cases, a very inconvenient inequality in the whole of the advantages and disadvantages of their different employments.
p96.zh: 第三,欧洲的政策阻碍劳动力和股票的自由流通,从就业到就业,以及从地方到地方,在某些情况下,它们不同就业的利弊总体上非常不方便。

p97.original: The statute of apprenticeship obstructs the free circulation of labour from one employment to another, even in the same place. The exclusive privileges of corporations obstruct it from one place to another, even in the same employment.
p97.zh: 学徒法规阻碍劳工从一个职业到另一个职业的自由流通,即使在同一地点也是如此.公司的专属特权阻碍它从一个地方到另一个地方,即使在同一就业岗位上也是如此。

p98.original: It frequently happens, that while high wages are given to the workmen in one manufacture, those in another are obliged to content themselves with bare subsistence. The one is in an advancing state, and has therefore a continual demand for new hands; the other is in a declining state, and the superabundance of hands is continually increasing. Those two manufactures may sometimes be in the same town, and sometimes in the same neighbourhood, without being able to lend the least assistance to one another. The statute of apprenticeship may oppose it in the one case, and both that and an exclusive corporation in the other. In many different manufactures, however, the operations are so much alike, that the workmen could easily change trades with one another, if those absurd laws did not hinder them. The arts of weaving plain linen and plain silk, for example, are almost entirely the same. That of weaving plain woollen is somewhat different; but the difference is so insignificant, that either a linen or a silk weaver might become a tolerable workman in a very few days. If any of those three capital manufactures, therefore, were decaying, the workmen might find a resource in one of the other two which was in a more prosperous condition; and their wages would neither rise too high in the thriving, nor sink too low in the decaying manufacture. The linen manufacture, indeed, is in England, by a particular statute, open to every body; but as it is not much cultivated through the greater part of the country, it can afford no general resource to the work men of other decaying manufactures, who, wherever the statute of apprenticeship takes place, have no other choice, but dither to come upon the parish, or to work as common labourers; for which, by their habits, they are much worse qualified than for any sort of manufacture that bears any resemblance to their own. They generally, therefore, chuse to come upon the parish.
p98.zh: 经常发生的情况是,虽然在一种制造中向工人发放高工资,但另一种制造中工人却不得不满足于赤裸裸的生活。前者处于进步状态,因此对新手的需求持续;后者处于衰落状态,手的超丰度在持续增加.这两种制造可能有时在同一城镇,有时在同一街区,无法相互提供最少的援助。学徒章程在一种情况下可以反对,而这种和另一种情况下的独家公司都可以反对。 然而,在许多不同的制造中,操作是完全相同的,如果这些荒谬的法律不阻碍它们,工人可以轻易地改变彼此之间的交易。 例如,编织平底亚麻和平底丝的艺术几乎完全相同。编织平庸的羊毛莲的区别有些不同;但差别很小,以至于亚麻或丝织在短短几天内可能成为可以忍受的工人. 因此,如果这三种资本制造中的任何一种正在腐烂,工人可能会在另外两种情况下找到一种资源,这种资源处于更繁荣的状态;他们的工资在繁荣的制造业中既不会上涨太高,也不会下降太低。麻布的制造,的确在英国,根据特定的法规,对每个身体都开放;但是由于它没有通过国家大部种植太多,它不能向其他腐烂的制造的工人提供一般资源,无论在哪里实行学徒制,他们别无选择,只能来到教区工作,或者做普通工人;根据他们的习惯,他们比任何一种与自己有相似之处的制造能力要差得多。 因此,他们一般会来到教区。

p99.original: Whatever obstructs the free circulation of labour from one employment to another, obstructs that of stock likewise; the quantity of stock which can be employed in any branch of business depending very much upon that of the labour which can be employed in it. Corporation laws, however, give less obstruction to the free circulation of stock from one place to another, than to that of labour. It is everywhere much easier for a wealthy merchant to obtain the privilege of trading in a town-corporate, than for a poor artificer to obtain that of working in it.
p99.zh: 无论什么阻碍劳工从一个行业自由流动到另一个行业,都同样阻碍库存的自由流动;任何行业部门都可以雇用的库存数量在很大程度上取决于可受雇于该行业的劳动力数量。 然而,公司法律对股票从一个地方到另一个地方的自由流通的阻碍比对劳工的阻碍要小。富裕的商人在任何地方都更容易获得在城镇公司进行交易的特权,比贫穷的艺术家更容易获得在其中工作的机会。

p100.original: The obstruction which corporation laws give to the free circulation of labour is common, I believe, to every part of Europe. That which is given to it by the poor laws is, so far as I know, peculiar to England. It consists in the difficulty which a poor man finds in obtaining a settlement, or even in being allowed to exercise his industry in any parish but that to which he belongs. It is the labour of artificers and manufacturers only of which the free circulation is obstructed by corporation laws. The difficulty of obtaining settlements obstructs even that of common labour. It may be worth while to give some account of the rise, progress, and present state of this disorder, the greatest, perhaps, of any in the police of England.
p100.zh: 我认为,公司法律对劳动力自由流动造成的阻碍,对欧洲各地来说都是常见的。 据我所知, 可怜的法律赋予它的东西 是英国特有的。 它包括穷人在获得安置时所遇到的困难,甚至被允许在除他所属的任何教区从事他的行业。 只有艺术品制造者和制造商的劳动,自由流通才受到公司法律的阻碍。获得安置的困难甚至阻碍了普通劳动力的安置。 也许值得一提一下这种混乱的兴起、进步和现状, 也许是英国警察中最伟大的。

p101.original: When, by the destruction of monasteries, the poor had been deprived of the charity of those religious houses, after some other ineffectual attempts for their relief, it was enacted, by the 43d of Elizabeth, c. 2. that every parish should be bound to provide for its own poor, and that overseers of the poor should be annually appointed, who, with the church-wardens, should raise, by a parish rate, competent sums for this purpose.
p101.zh: 当由于修道院的破坏,穷人被剥夺了这些宗教房屋的慈善活动时,经过一些其他无效的救济努力,由伊丽莎白43d,c颁布.2. 每个教区必须照顾自己的穷人,每年应任命穷人的监督员,由他们与教区牧师一起为此目的按教区费率筹集合格款项。

p102.original: By this statute, the necessity of providing for their own poor was indispensably imposed upon every parish. Who were to be considered as the poor of each parish became, therefore, a question of some importance. This question, after some variation, was at last determined by the 13th and 14th of Charles II. when it was enacted, that forty days undisturbed residence should gain any person a settlement in any parish; but that within that time it should be lawful for two justices of the peace, upon complaint made by the church-wardens or overseers of the poor, to remove any new inhabitant to the parish where he was last legally settled; unless he either rented a tenement of ten pounds a-year, or could give such security for the discharge of the parish where he was then living, as those justices should judge sufficient.
p102.zh: 根据这项法规,必须照顾自己的穷人,这是每个教区都绝对必要的。 因此,应当把谁视为每个教区的穷人,成为一个具有一定重要性的问题。这个问题经过一些修改后,最后由查理二世颁布时的第13和第14条确定,40天无干扰的住所应让任何人在任何教区获得定居;但是,在这段时间内,两名治安官在教会领袖或监督官提出申诉后,可以合法地将任何新的居民驱逐到他最后合法定居的教区;除非他每年租下10英镑的租房,或者可以为他当时居住的教区遣散提供这种保障,因为法官们应作出充分判断。

p103.original: Some frauds, it is said, were committed in consequence of this statute; parish officers sometime's bribing their own poor to go clandestinely to another parish, and, by keeping themselves concealed for forty days, to gain a settlement there, to the discharge of that to which they properly belonged. It was enacted, therefore, by the 1st of James II. that the forty days undisturbed residence of any person necessary to gain a settlement, should be accounted only from the time of his delivering notice, in writing, of the place of his abode and the number of his family, to one of the church-wardens or overseers of the parish where he came to dwell.
p103.zh: 据说,由于这一法规,发生了一些欺诈行为;教区官员有时贿赂自己的穷人,让他们秘密去另一个教区,并在那里躲了四十天,以便在那里获得和解,从而解除他们理应属于他们的东西。 因此,詹姆斯二世第1世颁布,任何人获得和解所需的四十天无干扰住所,只应从他发出书面通知时,即其住所地点和家属人数,到他前来居住的教区的一名教堂牧师或监督员,进行记账。

p104.original: But parish officers, it seems, were not always more honest with regard to their own than they had been with regard to other parishes, and sometimes connived at such intrusions, receiving the notice, and taking no proper steps in consequence of it. As every person in a parish, therefore, was supposed to have an interest to prevent as much as possible their being burdened by such intruders, it was further enacted by the 3rd of William III. that the forty days residence should be accounted only from the publication of such notice in writing on Sunday in the church, immediately after divine service.
p104.zh: 但教区官员似乎并不总是比其他教区更诚实地对待自己的教区,有时会对这种入侵感到默许,收到通知,因此没有采取任何适当步骤。 因此,由于一个教区中的每一个人都应该有利益来尽可能防止他们受到这种入侵者的重负,威廉三世第3章进一步规定,40天的居住时间只应在礼拜日,即神灵服务后立即在教堂内以书面形式公布这种通知后进行核算.

p105.original: "After all," says Doctor Burn, "this kind of settlement, by continuing forty days after publication of notice in writing, is very seldom obtained; and the design of the acts is not so much for gaining of settlements, as for the avoiding of them by persons coming into a parish clandestinely, for the giving of notice is only putting a force upon the parish to remove. But if a person's situation is such, that it is doubtful whether he is actually removable or not, he shall, by giving of notice, compel the parish either to allow him a settlement uncontested, by suffering him to continue forty days, or by removing him to try the right."
p105.zh: "毕竟,伯恩医生说,"这种和解,在书面通知公布40天后继续,是很少得到的;而行为的设计,与其说是为了获得和解,不如说是为了躲过秘密进入教区的人,因为发出通知只会给教区带来驱赶的力量. 但是如果一个人的情况是这样,那么他是否真的可以搬家是值得怀疑的,他应该通过通知来迫使教区要么允许他达成无争议的和解,要么让他继续40天,要么把他赶走去尝试权利".

p106.original: This statute, therefore, rendered it almost impracticable for a poor man to gain a new settlement in the old way, by forty days inhabitancy. But that it might not appear to preclude altogether the common people of one' parish from ever establishing themselves with security in another, it appointed four other ways by which a settlement might be gained without any notice delivered or published. The first was, by being taxed to parish rates and paying them; the second, by being elected into an annual parish office, and serving in it a year; the third, by serving an apprenticeship in the parish; the fourth, by being hired into service there for a year, and continuing in the same service during the whole of it. Nobody can gain a settlement by either of the two first ways, but by the public deed of the whole parish, who are too well aware of the consequences to adopt any new-comer, who has nothing but his labour to support him, either by taxing him to parish rates, or by electing him into a parish office.
p106.zh: 因此,这项法规使得穷人几乎无法以旧方式在40天的居住时间里获得新的安置。 但是,它似乎并不完全排除一个教区的普通人民在另一个教区的安居乐业,它指定了其他四种方式,在不发出或公布任何通知的情况下,通过这些方式获得和解。 第一个是按教区税率征税并支付费用;第二个是选入年度教区办公室,并在其中任职一年;第三个是在教区担任学徒;第四个是受雇于该校一年,并在整个教区期间继续从事同一工作。任何人都无法通过最初两种方式获得和解,而是通过整个教区的公共契约,他们非常清楚后果,无法收养任何新来者,他们只能靠自己的劳动来维持生计,或者通过向教区征收费用,或者通过选举他担任教区职务。

p107.original: No married man can well gain any settlement in either of the two last ways. An apprentice is scarce ever married; and it is expressly enacted, that no married servant shall gain any settlement by being hired for a year. The principal effect of introducing settlement by service, has been to put out in a great measure the old fashion of hiring for a year; which before had been so customary in England, that even at this day, if no particular term is agreed upon, the law intends that every servant is hired for a year. But masters are not always willing to give their servants a settlement by hiring them in this manner; and servants are not always willing to be so hired, because, as every last settlement discharges all the foregoing, they might thereby lose their original settlement in the places of their nativity, the habitation of their parents and relations.
p107.zh: 任何已婚男子都不可能通过最后两种方式获得任何和解。学徒很少结过婚;而且明确规定,任何已婚仆人不得通过受雇一年获得任何和解。实行按服务方式安置的主要效果是,在很大程度上展现了一年的旧的雇用方式;这在英格兰以前是如此习惯的,即使到今天,如果不商定具体任期,法律也打算雇用每个仆人一年。 但主人并不总是愿意通过这样雇用他们来给仆人一个安置;仆人并不总是愿意被这样雇用,因为,由于每一个最后的安置都解除了上述所有条件,他们可能因此失去他们原先安置在他们地盘、父母的居住和关系的地方。

p108.original: No independent workman, it is evident, whether labourer or artificer, is likely to gain any new settlement, either by apprenticeship or by service. When such a person, therefore, carried his industry to a new parish, he was liable to be removed, how healthy and industrious soever, at the caprice of any churchwarden or overseer, unless he either rented a tenement of ten pounds a-year, a thing impossible for one who has nothing but his labour to live by, or could give such security for the discharge of the parish as two justices of the peace should judge sufficient.
p108.zh: 任何独立工人,无论是工人还是工匠,都不可能通过学徒或服务获得任何新的安置。 因此,当这个人将他的产业带到一个新的教区时,他可能会被赶走,无论他多么健康,多么勤奋,无论他是否在任何教区牧师或监督者的摆布下,除非他每年租下10磅的租房,这对于除了他的劳动之外没有其他生活能力的人来说是不可能做到的,或者能够为教区遣散提供这种保障,因为和平的两位法官应当作出足够的判断。

p109.original: What security they shall require, indeed, is left altogether to their discretion; but they cannot well require less than thirty pounds, it having been enacted, that the purchase even of a freehold estate of less than thirty pounds value, shall not gain any person a settlement, as not being sufficient for the discharge of the parish. But this is a security which scarce any man who lives by labour can give; and much greater security is frequently demanded.
p109.zh: 事实上,它们所要求的担保完全由它们自行决定;但是,它们不能完全需要不到30磅的,因为已经颁布,购买即使是价值不到30磅的自保财产,也不得因不足以解除教区义务而获得任何个人的和解。 但是,这种保障是任何靠劳动生活的人都难以得到的;人们常常要求更大的保障。

p110.original: In order to restore, in some measure, that free circulation of labour which those different statutes had almost entirely taken away, the invention of certificates was fallen upon. By the 8th and 9th of William III. it was enacted that if any person should bring a certificate from the parish where he was last legally settled, subscribed by the church-wardens and overseers of the poor, and allowed by two justices of the peace, that every other parish should be obliged to receive him; that he should not be removable merely upon account of his being likely to become chargeable, but only upon his becoming actually chargeable; and that then the parish which granted the certificate should be obliged to pay the expense both of his maintenance and of his removal. And in order to give the most perfect security to the parish where such certificated man should come to reside, it was further enacted by the same statute, that he should gain no settlement there by any means whatever, except either by renting a tenement of ten pounds a-year, or by serving upon his own account in an annual parish office for one whole year; and consequently neither by notice nor by service, nor by apprenticeship, nor by paying parish rates. By the 12th of Queen Anne, too, stat. 1, c.18, it was further enacted, that neither the servants nor apprentices of such certificated man should gain any settlement in the parish where he resided under such certificate.
p110.zh: 为了在某种程度上恢复这些不同法规几乎完全取消的劳动力自由流动,证书的发明受到了挫折。至威廉三世第八世和第九世颁布,如果任何人从他最后合法定居的教区拿一份经教会牧师和穷人监督官签署,并得到两位治安官允许的证书,则所有其他教区都有义务接受他;他不应仅仅因为有可能成为可收费人而被迁移,而只有在他实际上成为可收费人时;然后,颁发证书的教区必须支付他的赡养费和被迁移的费用。 为了给这些有证书的人住在那里的教区提供最完美的保障,同一法规进一步规定,他不得在那里以任何方式获得任何安置,除非每年租10英镑的租房,或一年在一年的教区办公室自费工作;因此,既不得通过通知、服务、学徒或支付教区费用。至皇后安氏十二世,亦为司徒. 此外,还颁布了第1条(c.18)款,规定经认证的男子的仆人或学徒不得在根据该证书居住的教区获得任何安置。

p111.original: How far this invention has restored that free circulation of labour, which the preceding statutes had almost entirely taken away, we may learn from the following very judicious observation of Doctor Burn. "It is obvious," says he, "that there are divers good reasons for requiring certificates with persons coming to settle in any place; namely, that persons residing under them can gain no settlement, neither by apprenticeship, nor by service, nor by giving notice, nor by paying parish rates; that they can settle neither apprentices nor servants; that if they become chargeable, it is certainly known whither to remove them, and the parish shall be paid for the removal, and for their maintenance in the mean time; and that, if they fall sick, and cannot be removed, the parish which gave the certificate must maintain them; none of all which can be without a certificate. Which reasons will hold proportionably for parishes not granting certificates in ordinary cases; for it is far more than an equal chance, but that they will have the certificated persons again, and in a worse condition." The moral of this observation seems to be, that certificates ought always to be required by the parish where any poor man comes to reside, and that they ought very seldom to be granted by that which he purposes to leave. "There is somewhat of hardship in this matter of certificates," says the same very intelligent author, in his History of the Poor Laws, "by putting it in the power of a parish officer to imprison a man as it were for life, however inconvenient it may be for him to continue at that place where he has had the misfortune to acquire what is called a settlement, or whatever advantage he may propose himself by living elsewhere."
p111.zh: 这一发明在多大程度上恢复了上述法规几乎完全取消的劳动力自由流动,我们可以从伯恩医生的以下非常明智的观察中吸取教训。 他说,“很明显,要求向前来任何地方定居的人发放证书有各种理由;即居住在他们下面的人既不能通过学徒、服务、通知或支付教区费率获得任何解决办法;他们既不能安置学徒,也不能支付教区费率;如果他们成为收费人,当然知道他们在哪里可以搬走,教区在平均时间内就应当为搬走和生活费支付;如果他们生病,不能搬走,则颁发证书的教区必须维持他们;没有证明,所有这一切都不能得到。教区在普通情况下不颁发证书的原因何在? 因为这远不止一个平等的机会,而是他们将再次获得证书的人,而且条件更差。” 这一看法的道德观点似乎是,任何穷人的居住地点的教区必须始终要求颁发证书,他们很少得到他打算离开的地方。"这个证书问题有些困难",同一位非常聪明的作者在他的"穷法律史"中说,"通过将监禁一个人的权力置于教区官员的权力中,如同终身监禁一样,不管他多么不方便,他都可能继续在他不幸获得所谓和解的地方,或者他通过生活在别处而可能提出的任何好处".

p112.original: Though a certificate carries along with it no testimonial of good behaviour, and certifies nothing but that the person belongs to the parish to which he really does belong, it is altogether discretionary in the parish officers either to grant or to refuse it. A mandamus was once moved for, says Doctor Burn, to compel the church-wardens and overseers to sign a certificate; but the Court of King's Bench rejected the motion as a very strange attempt.
p112.zh: 虽然证书上没有关于良好行为的证明,而且只证明此人属于他真正所属的教区,但教区官员完全可以自行决定给予或拒绝。伯恩医生说,曾经有人动过一个曼达穆斯,强迫教会牧师和监理签署证书;但国王座法庭拒绝了这项动议,认为这是一次非常奇怪的尝试。

p113.original: The very unequal price of labour which we frequently find in England, in places at no great distance from one another, is probably owing to the obstruction which the law of settlements gives to a poor man who would carry his industry from one parish to another without a certificate. A single man, indeed who is healthy and industrious, may sometimes reside by sufferance without one; but a man with a wife and family who should attempt to do so, would, in most parishes, be sure of being removed; and, if the single man should afterwards marry, he would generally be removed likewise. The scarcity of hands in one parish, therefore, cannot always be relieved by their superabundance in another, as it is constantly in Scotland, and I believe, in all other countries where there is no difficulty of settlement. In such countries, though wages may sometimes rise a little in the neighbourhood of a great town, or wherever else there is an extraordinary demand for labour, and sink gradually as the distance from such places increases, till they fall back to the common rate of the country; yet we never meet with those sudden and unaccountable differences in the wages of neighbouring places which we sometimes find in England, where it is often more difficult for a poor man to pass the artificial boundary of a parish, than an arm of the sea, or a ridge of high mountains, natural boundaries which sometimes separate very distinctly different rates of wages in other countries.
p113.zh: 在英格兰,在彼此距离不远的地方,我们经常发现劳动力价格非常不平等,这可能是由于定居点法对一个穷人的阻挠,他没有证书就把他的产业从一个教区带到另一个教区。单身男子,确实健康而勤奋,有时可能因遭受痛苦而无一人居住;但妻子和家人应努力这样做的男子,在大多数教区,会确信被驱离;如果单身男子婚后结婚,一般也会被驱离。 因此,在一个教区,手紧不能总是因为在另一个教区内手紧而松懈,因为苏格兰和我认为,在解决问题没有困难的所有其他国家,手紧是经常存在的。 在这些国家,虽然工资有时在一个大城镇的居民区,或者在其他地方,对劳动力的需求特别大,随着这些地方的距离的扩大,工资可能略有上升,并逐渐下降,直到它们回到国家的共同比率;然而,我们从未遇到我们有时在英格兰发现的邻近地区工资中突然和不负责任的差异,因为在那里,穷人通过一个堂区的人为边界往往比海臂或高山山脊更困难,而高山脊有时在其他国家工资标准上差别很大。

p114.original: To remove a man who has committed no misdemeanour, from the parish where he chooses to reside, is an evident violation of natural liberty and justice. The common people of England, however, so jealous of their liberty, but like the common people of most other countries, never rightly understanding wherein it consists, have now, for more than a century together, suffered themselves to be exposed to this oppression without a remedy. Though men of reflection, too, have some times complained of the law of settlements as a public grievance; yet it has never been the object of any general popular clamour, such as that against general warrants, an abusive practice undoubtedly, but such a one as was not likely to occasion any general oppression. There is scarce a poor man in England, of forty years of age, I will venture to say, who has not, in some part of his life, felt himself most cruelly oppressed by this ill-contrived law of settlements.
p114.zh: 将一个没有犯过轻罪的人从他选择居住的教区驱逐出去,显然侵犯了自然自由和正义。 然而,英格兰的普通人民如此嫉妒他们的自由,但与大多数其他国家的普通人民一样,他们从未正确理解它所包括的地方,在一个多世纪以来,他们一起遭受这种压迫,却得不到补救。 虽然反省者有时也抱怨定居点法是公众的冤情;但是,它从未成为任何普遍群众的呼声的对象,例如针对普通搜查令的呼声,毫无疑问是一种虐待做法,但这种做法不会引起任何普遍压迫。英国几乎没有一个四十岁的穷人,我冒昧地说,他一生中有些时候没有感到自己受到这种不合情理的定居法的最残酷压迫。

p115.original: I shall conclude this long chapter with observing, that though anciently it was usual to rate wages, first by general laws extending over the whole kingdom, and afterwards by particular orders of the justices of peace in every particular county, both these practices have now gone entirely into disuse. "By the experience of above four hundred years," says Doctor Burn, "it seems time to lay aside all endeavours to bring under strict regulations, what in its own nature seems incapable of minute limitation; for if all persons in the same kind of work were to receive equal wages, there would be no emulation, and no room left for industry or ingenuity."
p115.zh: 在结束这一漫长的篇章时,我要指出,虽然在古代,工资是通常的,但首先根据适用于整个王国的一般法律,然后根据每个特定郡的和平法官的特别命令,这两种做法现在都完全不再使用。伯恩医生说,“根据400年以上的经验,似乎应该放弃所有努力, 来严格管理, 这本身的本质似乎无法限制分钟; 因为如果所有从事同样工作的人都能得到同等的工资,

p116.original: Particular acts of parliament, however, still attempt sometimes to regulate wages in particular trades, and in particular places. Thus the 8th of George III. prohibits, under heavy penalties, all master tailors in London, and five miles round it, from giving, and their workmen from accepting, more than two shillings and sevenpence halfpenny a-day, except in the case of a general mourning. Whenever the legislature attempts to regulate the differences between masters and their workmen, its counsellors are always the masters. When the regulation, therefore, is in favour of the workmen, it is always just and equitable; but it is sometimes otherwise when in favour of the masters. Thus the law which obliges the masters in several different trades to pay their workmen in money, and not in goods, is quite just and equitable. It imposes no real hardship upon the masters. It only obliges them to pay that value in money, which they pretended to pay, but did not always really pay, in goods. This law is in favour of the workmen; but the 8th of George III. is in favour of the masters. When masters combine together, in order to reduce the wages of their workmen, they commonly enter into a private bond or agreement, not to give more than a certain wage, under a certain penalty. Were the workmen to enter into a contrary combination of the same kind, not to accept of a certain wage, under a certain penalty, the law would punish them very severely; and, if it dealt impartially, it would treat the masters in the same manner. But the 8th of George III. enforces by law that very regulation which masters sometimes attempt to establish by such combinations. The complaint of the workmen, that it puts the ablest and most industrious upon the same footing with an ordinary workman, seems perfectly well founded.
p116.zh: 然而,议会的特定行为有时仍然试图管理特定行业和特定地点的工资。 因此,乔治三世的第八世禁止伦敦所有裁缝主裁,并禁止其五里外,每天给2先令和7便士半便士以上,除非是一般的哀悼.每当立法机关试图调节主人和工人之间的差别时,其顾问总是主人。 因此,当该条例有利于工人时,它总是公正和平等的;但有时却有利于主人。 因此,要求若干不同行业的主人以金钱而不是货物支付工人工资的法律是相当公正和平等的。令诸师子无实际苦恼. 它只要求它们以金钱支付这种价值,它们假装以商品支付,但并不总是真正支付。 此法偏于工夫;但佐治三世八世偏于工夫. 当主人公们联合起来时,为了降低工人的工资,他们通常会签订私人债券或协议,不给超过一定工资,受到一定的处罚. 如果工人在某种情况下采取相反的同种组合,不接受某一工资,则法律将予以严厉惩罚;如果处理公正,将给予主人同样的待遇。 但是乔治三世的第八世通过法律执行 那种规范,有时会试图通过这种组合来建立工人们抱怨说,它使最能干和最勤奋的人与普通工人处于同样的地位,这似乎有充分的理由。

p117.original: In ancient times, too, it was usual to attempt to regulate the profits of merchants and other dealers, by regulating the price of provisions and ether goods. The assize of bread is, so far as I know, the only remnant of this ancient usage. Where there is an exclusive corporation, it may, perhaps, be proper to regulate the price of the first necessary of life; but, where there is none, the competition will regulate it much better than any assize. The method of fixing the assize of bread, established by the 31st of George II. could not be put in practice in Scotland, on account of a defect in the law, its execution depending upon the office of clerk of the market, which does not exist there. This defect was not remedied till the third of George III. The want of an assize occasioned no sensible inconveniency; and the establishment of one in the few places where it has yet taken place has produced no sensible advantage. In the greater part of the towns in Scotland, however, there is an incorporation of bakers, who claim exclusive privileges, though they are not very strictly guarded. The proportion between the different rates, both of wages and profit, in the different employments of labour and stock, seems not to be much affected, as has already been observed, by the riches or poverty, the advancing, stationary, or declining state of the society. Such revolutions in the public welfare, though they affect the general rates both of wages and profit, must, in the end, affect them equally in all different employments. The proportion between them, therefore, must remain the same, and cannot well be altered, at least for any considerable time, by any such revolutions.
p117.zh: 在古代,人们也经常试图通过管制规定和乙醚货物的价格来管制商人和其他经销商的利润。 据我所知,面包的尺寸是这种古老用途的唯一残余。 在有排他性公司的地方,也许应该管制生命中第一个必要条件的价格;但是,如果没有这种条件,竞争将比任何规模强得多。乔治二世31日确立的面包大小的定型方法在苏格兰无法实践,因为法律存在缺陷,其执行取决于市场书记官的办公室,而那里并不存在. 这一缺陷直到乔治三世的第三年才得到纠正.规模庞大的匮乏没有引起合理的不便;在尚未出现这种情况的少数地方建立规模大小的匮乏并没有产生任何合理的优势。 然而,在苏格兰的大部分城镇,都有面包师的注册,他们要求享有专属特权,尽管他们并没有受到非常严格的保护.不同工资和利润比例在不同的劳动力和存量就业中的比例似乎没有受到多少影响,正如已经观察到的那样,社会财富或贫困、进步、固定或衰退状况都影响不大。公共福利方面的这种革命虽然影响到工资和利润的一般比率,但最终必须平等地影响到所有不同职业。 因此,它们之间的比例必须保持不变,而且至少在相当长的时间内不能被任何这种革命改变。
